Using satellite-derived annual GPP from 1982 to 2018, we combined ensemble empirical mode decomposition with Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify interannual, trend, and overall stability and assess variable importance, nonlinear associations, and local contributions. Results showed that: (1) Variable importance was strongly timescale-dependent. Interannual stability was most strongly associated with shortwave radiation trend (SRAD_SLOPE) and mean population density (POP_MEAN); trend stability with temperature variability (TEM_CV), SRAD_SLOPE, and POP_MEAN; and overall stability with SRAD_SLOPE and TEM_CV. Locally, SRAD_SLOPE (34.27%) and POP_MEAN (21.85%) were the main variables of interannual stability, TEM_CV (44.22%) of trend stability, and SRAD_SLOPE (50.68%) and TEM_CV (24.32%) of overall stability. (2) Associations varied across dimensions. Increasing precipitation was associated with higher trend stability but lower interannual and overall stability; SRAD_SLOPE was negatively associated with all three dimensions; and elevation, represented by the digital elevation model (DEM), showed opposite associations with trend stability and the other two dimensions. POP_MEAN showed a nonlinear association with trend stability, while forests and croplands were more closely associated with interannual and trend stability, respectively. Among land-cover trajectory types, no-significant-change trajectories in forests and grasslands were associated with higher interannual stability, whereas decrease-to-increase trajectories were associated with higher trend stability across all land-cover types. (3) Local SHAP patterns were spatially heterogeneous. SRAD_SLOPE and TEM_CV showed broadly similar patterns across dimensions, whereas PPT_SLOPE and DEM showed contrasting patterns between trend and interannual stability. These findings highlight the need to consider both temporal dimensions and spatial context when attributing dryland GPP stability and may inform future carbon-sink management.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns of vegetation drought responses in southern China revealed by multi-band vegetation optical depth
abstract: Global warming and the increasing frequency of extreme climate events have intensified the risks of seasonal and compound droughts in southern China. These changes have made vegetation water status respond to drought stress in more complex ways. However, we still lack a systematic understanding of how vegetation in southern China responds to atmospheric drought stress and soil moisture variations, and how these responses change over time. To address this gap, this study used C-, X-, CXKu-, Ku-, and L-band vegetation optical depth (VOD) data to characterize vegetation water status. Standardized vapor pressure deficit (NVPD), derived from air and dew-point temperatures, and standardized soil moisture anomalies (NSWD) were used to represent atmospheric drought stress and soil moisture conditions. Sliding-window regression, trend analysis, nonlinear dependence, lag identification, and path-effect analysis were applied to compare vegetation drought responses across VOD bands. Based on the comparative results, a representative VOD band was selected for long-term analysis of trends and abrupt changes in drought response sensitivity. The results revealed clear differences in drought responses among VOD bands. CXKu-band VOD exhibited the most ecologically consistent drought responses, with negative sensitivity to atmospheric drought stress and positive sensitivity to soil moisture availability. Its sensitivity to these two factors strengthened over time in 60.8% and 65.04% of valid pixels, respectively. Vegetation exhibited stronger nonlinear dependence on soil moisture than on atmospheric drought stress, with mean distance correlation coefficients of 0.37 and 0.30, respectively. Path effect analysis suggested a negative relationship between atmospheric drought stress and vegetation water status, while the relationship with soil moisture varied across VOD bands. Only CXKu-band VOD suggested a weak indirect association between atmospheric drought stress and vegetation water status through soil moisture. Long-term VOD analysis revealed that change points were concentrated during 2005–2010, with larger shifts in sensitivity to soil moisture than to atmospheric drought stress. Overall, vegetation drought responses may be shaped by atmospheric drought stress, soil moisture, and vegetation characteristics. CXKu-band VOD shows potential for monitoring vegetation water dynamics and drought responses in humid southern China.

title: EraseAnything++: Enabling Concept Erasure in Rectified Flow Transformers Leveraging Multi-Object Optimization
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Removing undesired concepts from large-scale text-to-image (T2I) and text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models-while preserving overall generative quality-remains a major challenge, particularly as modern models such as Stable Diffusion v3, Flux, and OpenSora employ flow-matching and transformer-based architectures, as well as extending to long-horizon video generation. Existing concept erasure methods, designed for earlier T2I/T2V models, often fail to generalize to these paradigms. To address this, we propose EraseAnything++, a unified framework for concept erasure in both image and video diffusion models with flow-matching objectives. Central to our approach is formulating concept erasure as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem, explicitly balancing concept removal with the preservation of generative utility. To solve such problem with conflicting objectives, we introduce an efficient utility-preserving unlearning strategy based on implicit gradient surgery. Furthermore, by integrating LoRA-based parameter tuning with attention-level regularization, our method anchors erasure on key visual representations and propagates it consistently across spatial and temporal dimensions. In the video setting, we further enhance consistency through an anchor-and-propagate mechanism, which initializes erasure on reference frames and enforces it throughout subsequent transformer layers, thereby mitigating temporal drift. Extensive experiments on both image and video benchmarks demonstrate that EraseAnything++ substantially outperforms prior methods in erasure effectiveness, generative fidelity, and temporal consistency, establishing a new state of the art for concept erasure in next-generation diffusion models.

title: Q-Zoom: Query-Aware Adaptive Perception for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) require high-resolution visual inputs for fine-grained tasks like document understanding and dense scene perception. However, current global resolution scaling paradigms indiscriminately flood the quadratic self-attention mechanism with visually redundant tokens, severely bottlenecking inference throughput while ignoring spatial sparsity and query intent. To overcome this, we propose Q-Zoom, a query-aware adaptive high-resolution perception framework that operates in an efficient coarse-to-fine manner. First, a lightweight Dynamic Gating Network adaptively bypasses high-resolution processing when coarse global features suffice. Second, for queries demanding fine-grained perception, a Self-Distilled Region Proposal Network (SD-RPN) localizes the task-relevant Region-of-Interest (RoI) directly from intermediate feature spaces. To optimize these modules efficiently, the gating network uses a consistency-aware generation strategy to derive routing labels, while the SD-RPN employs a fully self-supervised distillation paradigm. A continuous spatio-temporal alignment scheme and targeted fine-tuning then fuse the dense local RoI with the coarse global layout. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-Zoom establishes a new Pareto frontier. Using Qwen2.5-VL-7B as a primary testbed, Q-Zoom accelerates inference by $2.5\times$ on Document & OCR benchmarks and $4.7\times$ in High-Resolution scenarios in accuracy-matched comparisons against the baseline's peak-accuracy token budget. Furthermore, at its largest visual-token budget, Q-Zoom surpasses the baseline's peak performance by 1.1% and 8.1% on these respective benchmarks, while keeping about $0.8\times$ of the base model's throughput at a matched token budget. These robust improvements transfer consistently to LLaVA, Qwen3-VL, encoder-free Gemma-4, and RL-based thinking-with-image models.

title: Preserving Geometric Integrity in Graph Prompting Via Measure-Constrained Optimal Transport
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Graph prompt learning enables parameter-efficient adaptation of frozen Graph Neural Networks to downstream tasks through lightweight prompt parameters. As routing becomes increasingly node-adaptive, however, independently optimized local decisions can collectively concentrate assignment mass on a small subset of a finite shared prompt bank, even when individual node-prompt matches remain locally meaningful. We propose MINT (Measure-INtegrity Transport), an entropically regularized optimal transport framework that formulates node-to-prompt adaptation as a globally coupled allocation problem. The transport cost favors local geometric compatibility, while a prescribed prompt-side marginal explicitly controls graph-wide prompt utilization. We further derive an exact variance decomposition that separates prompt-side geometric variance into retained prompt-update variation and within-node barycentric dispersion, together with a conditional stability bound for the frozen-encoder forward map. Across standard citation networks and additional heterophilic graphs, MINT remains competitive in few-shot adaptation. Controlled and end-to-end experiments further distinguish the roles of routing and topology: fixed-marginal routing controls graph-wide prompt utilization and has measurable end-to-end effects on citation networks, while topology augmentation provides a complementary, graph-dependent mechanism for addressing structural mismatch.

title: Heavy-Tailed Distributed Kernel Regression via Adaptive Huberization and Nyström Sketching
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: This paper develops a distributed RKHS method for nonparametric mean regression when noise is heavy-tailed. The estimator couples adaptive Huber loss with stagewise surrogate correction and projects both the master optimization and the communicated worker gradients into a shared Nyström subspace. This coordinated design preserves projected first-order agreement while reducing each worker message to an $m$-dimensional summary. We analyze the resulting multi-stage recursion under finite $(1+\delta )$ moments and show how contraction, regularization bias, truncation bias, stochastic fluctuation, and sketch approximation enter the final error bound. The theory is also extended to the case with arbitrarily contaminated responses. Numerical results confirm the robustness and efficiency of the proposed method.

title: MPC-Net: A Physics-Coupled Deep Learning Framework for Boundary Layer Parameterization Correction in Radiation Fog
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Conventional planetary boundary layer (PBL) schemes struggle to capture turbulence structures within foggy boundary layers, leading to significant biases in fog formation and evolution, especially under stable nocturnal conditions and complex terrain. Consequently, such schemes often fail to accurately reproduce the timing, intensity, and spatial distribution of radiation fog. This study proposes a Multiscale Physics-Coupled Correction Network (MPC-Net) that post-processes 3-D atmospheric fields simulated by the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model with conventional PBL schemes. Using a dual-branch heterogeneous network with spatiotemporal attention, MPC-Net learns discrepancies across multiple PBL schemes and their nonlinear mapping to large-eddy simulation (LES) turbulence characteristics. The model separately extracts thermo-dynamic and cloud-phase features, and incorporates physics-informed constraints to improve dynamical consistency. Experimental results show that MPC-Net outperforms conventional schemes, reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) for visibility, liquid water content (LWC), and liquid water path (LWP) by 73.3%, 60.0%, and 66.7%, respectively, over the YSU scheme baseline. The framework improves the spatial reconstruction of fog distribution, temporal stability of fog evolution, and physical consistency in key boundary layer variables. By learning radiation fog physics to correct biases in PBL-scheme outputs, this work offers a new approach for high-resolution fog forecasting.

title: Learning Adaptive Two-Stream One-Stage Vision Transformers for Real-Time UAV Tracking
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: By unifying feature extraction and search-template interaction to enable early target perception, one-stage trackers have become increasingly popular compared to two-stream trackers. However, most of these trackers adopt a complete vision transformer (ViT) architecture and overlook the inherent layer redundancy in ViTs, resulting in intensive feature computations that burden resource-constrained unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). To address this issue, we propose a real-time UAV tracker, namely SGLATrack, which adaptively optimizes redundant ViT layers according to tracking scenes via a similarity-guided layer adaptation (SGLA) approach. Despite achieving certain efficiency gains, SGLATrack is still constrained by repeated template feature extraction inherent to one-stage architectures. Reverting to a conventional two-stream architecture can avoid this issue and cache template features, but inevitably sacrifices the early target perception capability of one-stage trackers. To address this trade-off, we further propose SGLATrackV2 by introducing an adaptive two-stream one-stage framework that reorganizes the tracking pipeline into two complementary branches. Specifically, the first branch is only activated in the initial frame to cache template features, avoiding repeated feature extraction and retaining the efficiency advantage of two-stream architectures. The second branch jointly performs search feature extraction and search-template interaction in subsequent frames, preserving the early target perception capability of one-stage architectures. Moreover, the proposed SGLA approach is seamlessly integrated into the second branch to adaptively optimize redundant feature interactions. Consequently, the proposed framework unifies template caching, early target perception, and adaptive relation modeling within a single architecture. Beyond the frameworklevel improvements, a lightweight temporal learning mechanism is introduced to enhance tracking robustness in complex UAV scenarios. This mechanism is tailored for UAV tracking and can mine the changing patterns of targets in video streams with negligible computational overhead by selectively propagating finegrained object appearance tokens. Extensive experimental results on eight aerial datasets demonstrate that SGLATrackV2 achieves excellent performance in both tracking speed and precision.

title: Evolutionary Semi-supervised Camouflaged Object Detection via Intra-Task Curriculum Continual Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Existing semi-supervised camouflaged object detection (SSCOD) methods typically use unified-set stochastic training, which mixes samples of varying learning difficulty without explicit data-flow organization. In camouflaged scenes, this undifferentiated training can amplify early pseudo-label confirmation bias from hard samples and dilute the gradients of hard samples in later stages, especially under heterogeneous difficulty distributions. To address this, we propose Intra-Task Curriculum Continual Learning (ICCL), a difficulty-aware dynamic curriculum data-flow framework for SSCOD. ICCL first employs an Intrinsic-Extrinsic Difficulty Estimator (IEDE) to construct an easy-to-hard curriculum using a low-weight distribution prior and model-feedback uncertainty. A Saturation-Driven Flow Scheduler (SDFS) then adaptively advances the curriculum and replaces saturated easy samples, maintaining an information-dense and efficient training stream. To stabilize non-stationary intra-task data flow, a Dual-Branch Knowledge Consolidator (DBKC) applies parameter regularization and prediction distillation. Additionally, Prompt-Guided Label Rectification (PGLR) serves as a pseudo-label quality-control module by refining and filtering noisy pseudo-labels with hybrid SAM prompts. Experiments show that ICCL achieves competitive or best performance under low-label conditions. Ablations show that ICCL remains effective without PGLR, while PGLR provides complementary gains through pseudo-label refinement. ICCL also reduces unlabeled-sample updates by 81.66% relative to standard unified-set training and shows promising cross-domain continual adaptation.

title: UrbanSeg: Spatial-aware Semantic Segmentation in Urban Scenes
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning, the semantic analysis in 3D urban scenes has gained paramount significance. However, diverse semantic objects in urban scenes take substantial challenges for semantic analysis and limit the practicality in downstream applications. In this paper, we propose a new semantic segmentation method UrbanSegto perceive such complex urban objects. It employs a voxel-based spatial analysis technique to enhance the generalization. Meanwhile, a redesigned spatial-aware network with point-based serialization is utilized in UrbanSeg to improve the perception of various urban objects with different scales and ambiguous geometric relationships. The experiment demonstrates that our method effectively enhances the practicality.

title: Weakly Supervised Contrastive Learning: Tackling Imprecise Labels with Theoretical Guarantees
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Contrastive learning has achieved remarkable success in representation learning, and supervised contrastive learning often outperforms its self-supervised counterpart. In practice, however, annotations are frequently ambiguous or inaccurate, so the observed labels may not reliably indicate whether two examples belong to the same class. This limits the applicability of conventional supervised contrastive learning. We address this problem by introducing continuous semantic similarity, which replaces hard positive-negative assignments with a continuously valued estimate of the probability that two examples share a class. We then formulate a graph-theoretic framework for weakly supervised contrastive learning in which examples are graph vertices and semantic similarities are edge weights. The framework applies to multiple forms of weak supervision and can be integrated with existing task-specific methods. Theoretically, we derive an error bound showing that, under mild conditions, the learned representation can approximate one obtained with full supervision. Empirical studies demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves consistent improvements in four weakly supervised learning settings: noisy label learning (NLL), partial label learning (PLL), semi-supervised learning (SSL), and noisy partial label learning (NPLL).

title: A 3D Simulator for Passive SPAD Imaging
abstract: Passive single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras provide short-exposure observations for low-light perception, but collecting task annotations for these sensors remains difficult, and annotated datasets are scarce. We present a 3D simulation pipeline that generates realistic photon detections together with camera-motion and semantic labels, enabling perception models to be trained on synthetic SPAD observations and applied directly to real-world data. The pipeline couples controllable scene geometry and motion with a sensor-informed observation model that accounts for photon shot noise, dark counts, and spatial crosstalk. We evaluate the pipeline through calibrated photon-count comparisons and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across three downstream perception tasks. We show that classifiers trained only on synthetic SPAD data achieve high accuracy on real low-light recordings at illumination levels less than 2 lux, without real-data fine-tuning. Similarly, we apply models trained entirely on simulated camera sweeps to real-world camera-rotation estimation and achieve mean absolute rotation errors of less than 1 degree on real 20-degree and 30-degree sweeps at 0.5 and 5.0 lux, when deployed zero-shot. We additionally train semantic segmentation models on synthetic data with automatically generated dense labels and perform direct inference on real-world low-light recordings; the results further demonstrate the usefulness of synthetic dense supervision for real low-light perception. Our simulator thus provides a practical source of annotated training data for real SPAD perception.

title: Memory as the Backbone: A Dual-Store Associative Memory Architecture for Visual Recognition
abstract: We investigate whether explicit memory can serve as the organizing principle of a general-purpose visual backbone. Inspired by the interaction between working and long-term memory in human cognition, we introduce DuSAM (Dual-Store Associative Memory), a hierarchical memory-native visual backbone coupling image-local working memory (WM) with a fixed-capacity persistent semantic memory (PM). WM organizes local visual evidence into compact, spatially anchored states that are updated and transported across stages, then read back to refine dense features. PM consolidates semantic evidence from training images and annotated regions into prototypes, whose retrieved content enriches the same working states. With these memory operations in place of self-attention or state-space blocks, DuSAM achieves competitive performance relative to representative, similarly sized backbones on ImageNet-1K classification, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and COCO object detection and instance segmentation. Ablations show contributions from both stores, with PM particularly benefiting class groups with fewer annotated training pixels. At $2048\times2048$, the complete DuSAM-based UPerNet segmentor achieves $2.36\times$ the throughput of the evaluated DeiT-S/16 counterpart while using $59.5\%$ less GPU memory, and $1.24\times$ the throughput of the linear-complexity VMamba-T. Memory analyses reveal spatially selective WM access and semantic associations between retrieved prototypes and training regions. Class-targeted removal and restoration further demonstrate that category-specific experience can be replenished through state updates without changing network parameters. These results establish explicit memory as a viable organizing principle for visual backbones and provide a foundation for jointly designing contextual computation and addressable semantic memory.

title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with non-convex polygonal neighborhoods: A hybrid Iterated Local Search--Block Coordinate Descent approach
abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) generalizes the classical TSP by requiring a tour to visit a set of regions in the Euclidean plane rather than fixed point coordinates. It has applications in last-mile delivery, surveillance, and remote sensing in precision agriculture. In this paper, we address the Euclidean TSPN with arbitrary, non-convex polygonal neighborhoods---a highly complex setting due to the joint continuous and combinatorial optimization challenges. To solve the continuous subproblem of determining optimal visit points for a given visiting sequence, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method based on solving fast one-dimensional geometric subproblems. Computational experiments demonstrate that BCD computes optimal visit points for a fixed sequence in almost all instances in which optimality is certified, more than six orders of magnitude faster than a commercial solver solving the equivalent Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Programming (MIQCP) formulation. This efficiency enables an effective hybrid Iterated Local Search metaheuristic (ILS-BCD) that thoroughly explores the combinatorial search space at low computational cost. Extensive computational tests on 235 benchmark instances derived from the Generalized TSP (GTSP), with up to 100 neighborhoods, show that ILS-BCD matched or improved upon the best-known GTSP tours in all cases, obtaining strictly shorter tours in 234 instances. On the 80 instances for which optimality is proven, ILS-BCD attains the optimal tour length in all of them, within a relative difference below 0.001%. On 60 larger instances, with as many as 6,325 neighborhoods, ILS-BCD remains competitive up to about 220.

title: Spectrify: Framework for Hyperspectral Image Generation Using Computer Graphics
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) record the full spectrum of light at every pixel, so projecting an HSI through a camera's spectral sensitivities gives that camera's RAW image, and one HSI can supply training data for hyperspectral reconstruction and camera-pipeline methods. Real HSIs, however, are slow and expensive to capture, and the largest datasets hold only about 1,000 images. High-level vision commonly replaces scarce real data with images rendered from 3D scenes. Low-level tasks, however, need physically correct spectra, which requires spectral rendering with a measured spectrum for every material in a scene, and existing spectral renderings cover only a handful of scenes, mostly with a simplified image formation model. We present Spectrify, a framework that converts 3D scene datasets into HSIs, together with a library of reflectance spectra labeled by material and compiled from close-range hyperspectral datasets and spectrophotometer measurements. In Spectrify, spectra follow the material: each object receives a physically based optical model and measured reflectance spectra or optical constants from its material category, each lamp an emission spectrum of its type and the sky a modeled daylight spectrum, and Mitsuba 3 path-traces the full light transport of each scene per wavelength. We show that a hyperspectral reconstruction network trained only on our synthetic HSIs generalizes to unseen real datasets better than networks trained on the largest real HSI datasets on most test sets, and that assigning spectra by material category instead of by color alone improves this transfer on every test set. RAW images projected from our HSIs are also useful training data for color constancy, performing on par with existing synthetic RAW generators. We release the 4,500 rendered HSIs, the code of Spectrify and its material-labeled reflectance library.

title: SHARPnP: Self-Supervised and Plug-and-Play Hyperspectral Super-Resolution from Real Noisy Unaligned Camera Measurements
abstract: Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise. Low-cost RGB cameras provide fine visible details to guide NIR reconstruction, but introduce spatially varying cross-camera misalignment. Supervised fusion methods require relatively large datasets of clean, high-resolution hyperspectral images, are sensitive to sensor noise, and generalize poorly across new sensors. We introduce SHARPnP, an interpretable, flexible framework coupling registration and reconstruction for RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy, unaligned measurements without clean references. We adapt a pretrained registration model via a cross-view loss backpropagated through a fixed plug-and-play fusion module. Temporal and recorrupted pairs enable reference-free self-supervision on noisy inputs. At test time, we calibrate cross-camera radiometry and refine alignment. Plug-and-play fusion employs sequential three-band denoising. On the REAL benchmark, SHARPnP outperforms supervised fusion baselines at $4\times$, $8\times$, and $16\times$ on clean inputs and at $4\times$ under Gaussian noise ($σ=5/255, 10/255$). On native RGB-HSI snapshot measurements, it reconstructs all 51 VIS-NIR bands, beyond the conventional 31-band VIS setting, without high-resolution references.

title: NEST: Uncovering and Nesting Unknown Objects in Open-World Object Detection
abstract: Open-world object detectors aim to localize objects of classes not covered by their training annotations, but most label them only as "unknown". This label tells a system that an object is present but not what it is, while its broader category would allow a more informed decision. We therefore address both uncovering unknown objects and assigning them to the broader categories of a given class taxonomy. For uncovering, we find that most unknown objects are already localized and labeled "unknown" in our base detector, but are discarded during final top-k selection because background receives higher scores. To mitigate this, we propose a class-agnostic ranker that estimates how well each predicted box fits an object and uses these scores to select the final predictions. Across three benchmarks, our detector improves unknown recall by 3.8% to 195.1% relative to the strongest baseline in each task, while maintaining competitive known-class detection. For categorizing, we draw on Euler diagrams, in which the region of a category contains the regions of its members. Our categorizer builds each category's region from the known classes and learns how much room to leave for members it has never seen. On the same detections, it categorizes unknown objects more accurately than existing hierarchical methods. Code is available at https://github.com/TUM-AVS/NEST.

title: Simultaneously Boosting Efficiency and Capability for Linear Attention via Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification
abstract: Self-attention's quadratic complexity constitutes a core bottleneck for Vision Transformers (ViTs). Existing efficiency-oriented optimizations, including softmax-based and linear attention (LA) variants, generally compromise model representational capacity, leading to inevitable performance degradation. We propose a novel linear attention which alleviates this efficiency-capability dilemma. For the first time, we embed an Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification (ACCAP) mechanism into the QKV projection of linear attention, which enables the model to retain high-dimensional feature information while performing computations with reduced channels. We further fuse a focused kernel function and a self-gating module into ACCAP to construct a lightweight linear attention module (ACCAP-LA). Our theoretical analysis shows that, compared to standard linear attention, ACCAP-LA reduces the attention module's parameter count by 79.17% and FLOPs by 77.5%. Extensive experiments demonstrate ACCAP-LA's effectiveness: when applied to ViT, it achieves 79.4% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with only 5.8M parameters, and more notably, it boasts strong cross-architecture compatibility, boosting EfficientViT-b1 and PVT-T by 3.3% and 3.4% respectively.

title: DOPER: Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited
abstract: We present DOPER, an RGB pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across object detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction to recover the 6D pose of known objects through Perspective-n-Point. Starting from synthetic training, DOPER adapts to real observations using partial supervision while retaining synthetic keypoint labels. Calibrated multi-view observations provide geometric constraints for keypoint supervision. During inference, optional heatmap refinement fits a rigid pose directly to the predicted keypoint distributions, resolving ambiguous correspondences without depth input or a learned pose refiner. Starting from underspecified CAD models, DOPER progressively refines the object representation and pose estimator. Results on SPEED+ and SHIRT further demonstrate effective adaptation to illumination changes and accurate temporal pose estimation. Across the evaluated single-view and multi-view configurations, DOPER achieves state-of-the-art detection AP results on HANDAL, HOPEv2, HOT3D, and T-LESS while using only RGB and running in real time (35 Hz per object model on one GB300). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of jointly learning detection and pose keypoints, with real observations and geometric constraints.

title: Beyond Static Semantics: Instance-Adaptive Vision-Language Alignment for Building Damage Assessment
abstract: Instance-level building damage assessment (IBDA) from bi-temporal remote sensing imagery remains challenging, as the same damage grade may exhibit diverse visual manifestations across individual buildings. Natural language offers explicit descriptions of physical damage, providing complementary semantic cues beyond discrete category labels. However, existing vision--language approaches have not fully addressed how damage semantics should adapt to local bi-temporal evidence and subsequently serve as instance-specific references for severity discrimination. To bridge this gap, we propose LAMIA-IBDA, a unified vision--language framework that progressively grounds shared damage semantics in local observations and individual buildings. Specifically, Adaptive Text-Visual Alignment (ATVA) enables evidence-adaptive semantic interaction by jointly contextualizing multiple damage descriptions and bi-temporal visual features under reliability-aware attention supervision. Dynamic Instance-Prototype Grounding (DIPG) further associates these contextualized semantics with individual building regions to construct instance-adaptive prototypes for fine-grained damage classification. Instance-level description preferences additionally supervise fusion-stage attention, linking semantic adaptation with instance discrimination. Extensive experiments on xBD and BRIGHT demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across optical--optical and optical--SAR settings. The source code is publicly available https://github.com/Cutensil/LAMIA-IBDA.

title: Seeing to Drive on a Single Board: Attention-Free Depth for Onboard Robot Navigation
abstract: A small ground robot can carry one camera and a few watts of compute, but the depth foundation models that could turn that camera into a range sensor are vision transformers sized for GPUs. We bring one to a Raspberry Pi 5 with the Hailo-8L, an accelerator that runs every layer in integer arithmetic, attention included. Quantised for it, Depth Anything V2 loses large parts of the scene, and we measure why: at 449 tokens, 91% of softmax weights fall below one int8 step while carrying 17-33% of the attention mass. Our answer is to distil, not quantise. An attention-free ResNet-34 U-Net student of Depth Anything V2-Large (24.5M parameters) runs at 27.1 FPS on the chip, its int8 output matches its float twin (Pearson 0.99993), and on held-out scenes of its simulated yard it is the most accurate depth network on the chip (AbsRel 0.269 against 0.354-0.530). On 1,000 stereo-verified points of a real outdoor drive it is not resolvably different from the vendor's Depth Anything V2-Small build, while running faster (27.1 vs 21.6 FPS). Ranging obstacles by where they meet the floor needs only the camera height, so mapping, hybrid-A* planning and SLAM run on the Pi's own CPU. In real-time hardware-in-the-loop tests in a Gaussian-splat reconstruction of a real yard, the stack reaches the goal without contact in 7.9$\pm$1.1 of 10 scenes, against 9.2$\pm$0.4 with exact obstacles, and in 7.7$\pm$0.7 on its own pose with simulated wheel odometry (ten seeds each; 8.2$\pm$0.4 with the real Pi and Hailo-8L in the loop, five seeds). The source code, pre-trained models and data are available at https://github.com/itaim18/DANIEL.

title: SplatSeg3D: Efficient Zero-Shot 3D Segmentation via Point Cloud Surfelization and Splatting
abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation methods rely on 2D foundation models applied to registered images captured alongside the 3D point clouds. However, such images may not be available in many cases, while direct 3D point cloud segmentation methods require semantic class supervision and are challenging to deploy in a zero-shot manner. To address these issues, we present SplatSeg3D, which segments a bare colored point cloud in an open-vocabulary manner without requiring the accompanying images, camera poses, class supervision, or instance mask proposals. To achieve this, we first surfelize the input point cloud and obtain oriented 2D Gaussians. We then render views of the scene by splatting, with a view selection strategy that maximizes scene coverage with as few views as possible. Next, we apply text-prompted segmentation on the rendered views, giving each 3D point a set of multi-view semantic cues, fused to produce a 3D segmentation of the scene. We evaluate SplatSeg3D on semantic segmentation and novel-class instance segmentation on 4 standard benchmarks: Scannet, Scannet++, Replica, and S3DIS. Our pipeline not only performs better or on-par with the state-of-the-art, but we also achieve these results efficiently across runtime and compute requirements. Code will be published.

title: On the Capabilities and Limitations of Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Cloud Segmentation
abstract: Recent advances in vision-language foundation models have enabled open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) without task-specific training, offering new opportunities for Earth Observation (EO) applications. However, their capabilities for cloud detection remain insufficiently explored. In this work, we evaluate twelve OVSS approaches across six publicly available EO datasets in a zero-shot setting, i.e., without fine-tuning or adaptation to the target data. We investigate both binary cloud detection and multiclass segmentation, distinguishing between thick clouds, thin clouds, cloud shadows, and background. Our results show differences in performance across models and datasets, with SegEarth-OV3 achieving the highest binary cloud detection performance on four of the six datasets. While several approaches demonstrate promising performance in binary cloud detection, multiclass segmentation remains more challenging, particularly when distinguishing between fine-grained cloud categories. Furthermore, our controlled prompt sensitivity analysis reveals model-dependent responses to alternative textual descriptions, with appearance-oriented prompts benefiting certain approaches while degrading the performance of others. Overall, our findings demonstrate both the potential and current limitations of zero-shot OVSS for cloud detection, establishing a comparative benchmark for future research on generalisable cloud segmentation. Code will be available at: https://github.com/josesosajs/zero-shot-cloudovss.

title: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness
abstract: A common occurrence in Large Language Models (LLMs) is the emergence of so-called massive activations. This phenomenon is well known in the literature and has been connected to attention sinks, representational compression, as well as signal propagation. However, the reasons and consequences for their appearance are not yet well understood. In this paper, we explain the role of massive activations in deep learning by showing that they are connected to the region migration phenomenon in delayed robustness. Under the spline theoretic interpretation of deep networks, we show that massive activations push the representations away from the nonlinearity boundaries of the network, decreasing the complexity of its input-output map around data points. Furthermore, we uncover for the first time that this phenomenon is not unique to transformers and actually appears in a number of common architectures performing simple supervised learning tasks. We validate this connection through extensive experiments on a diverse set of architectures including residual MLP, ResNet18, Vision Transformers and GPT and datasets including MNIST, CIFAR10, Imagenette and Shakespeare Text. We consistently observe that massive activations and region migration co-occur with adversarial robustness. Furthermore, we illustrate that this connection holds in the large-scale pretraining of LLMs by showing that the rise of massive activations in LLMs closely tracks the adversarial accuracy of the model under perturbations of the token embeddings.

title: Rescuing Discarded Boundary Samples in Semi-Supervised Learning
abstract: The field of semi-supervised learning (SSL) has seen substantial progress, driven by ongoing refinements within the pseudo-label SSL paradigm. The main difficulty lies in reducing the adverse impact of confirmation bias. The predominant approach is to apply a confidence threshold during training to discard low-confidence samples. Nevertheless, while this mitigates the bias, the discarded samples are mostly situated near class boundaries, and consequently, this strategy also loses valuable boundary information. To address this problem, we propose Boundary Refinement and Correction (BRC), an add-on for confidence-thresholded SSL that rescues useful discarded samples without changing how the base SSL method selects pseudo-labels. BRC keeps the original confidence-based selection rule and operates only on the rejected set. It first identifies discarded samples that may still be useful for training, then replaces their original pseudo-labels with corrected soft pseudo-labels and returns them to the unsupervised loss. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100, STL-10, and TissueMNIST demonstrate the flexibility and broad applicability of BRC across diverse datasets and base SSL methods, reducing error rates by up to 4.97 percentage points. On boundary-near samples, BRC further improves Top-1 accuracy by 12.80 percentage points, directly supporting its ability to refine the model's decision boundary. An exploratory extension to semantic segmentation also yields consistent gains of 1.03-2.39 mIoU, indicating that BRC generalizes beyond image classification.

title: Resource-Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Early Rice Blast Forecasting in Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Resource-efficient artificial intelligence has become increasingly important for sustainable agriculture, where timely disease forecasting must be achieved under computational and energy constraints. Early estimation of rice blast can enhance food security by optimizing crop management practices while reducing excessive pesticide use. However, existing frameworks often suffer from high computational overhead and limited capability to model the complex spectral-temporal dependencies present in heterogeneous meteorological and remote sensing data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a lightweight multimodal fusion framework comprising an attentive positional encoding-based Transformer and a convolutional neural network (CNN)-embedded gated recurrent unit (GRU) for efficient spectral-temporal representation learning. The attention-enhanced positional encoding assigns adaptive importance to sequential meteorological tokens, enabling effective modelling of temporal characteristics. In parallel, the lightweight CNN extracts discriminative spectral features, while the GRU captures temporal dynamics from remote sensing imagery acquired over two time-instances. A multimodal fusion layer integrates these heterogeneous representations to forecast rice blast risk 5-10 days before symptom manifestation across diverse agro-climatic zones. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a validation accuracy of 96.93% and an F1-score of 95.79%. In addition to its predictive performance, the lightweight multimodal architecture substantially reduces computational complexity, inference latency, and carbon emissions, making it an energy-efficient solution for large-scale disease forecasting. The proposed framework provides a practical foundation for resource-efficient artificial intelligence in sustainable agriculture.

title: HS-OVSeg: Multi-Granularity Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Heterogeneous Supervision
abstract: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) enables flexible, text-driven mapping of remote sensing (RS) imagery beyond predefined categories. Despite advances in segmentation foundation models, RS-OVSS remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, semantically diverse datasets with accurate pixel-level annotations. Meanwhile, existing RS datasets contain abundant scene- and object-level annotations that offer valuable semantic information but lack precise pixel-wise supervision. To exploit these complementary sources, we propose HS-OVSeg, a unified training framework that integrates heterogeneous scene-, object-, and pixel-level supervision for RS-OVSS. Specifically, we generate pixel-wise pseudo-labels using SAM3, conditioned on scene-level class names and object-level class names with bounding boxes. Combined with ground-truth semantic masks, these pseudo-labels enable joint training across all three annotation granularities through LoRA-based fine-tuning of SAM3. Our unified training spans 20 RS datasets, including 3 scene classification, 4 object detection, and 13 semantic segmentation datasets, with 1,000 images from the 7 classification and detection datasets manually annotated for pixel-level evaluation. HS-OVSeg substantially outperforms existing RS-OVSS models across both the 20 training-source and 5 held-out datasets, demonstrating strong multi-granularity segmentation capabilities under heterogeneous supervision. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

title: An Integrated Remote Sensing and Machine Learning Framework for Mapping Hazard Associated with Leached Metals
abstract: This study integrates satellite remote sensing, groundwater monitoring, and machine learning to map leached-metal-associated hazards at four coal combustion residual (CCR) sites in Virginia, USA. Constituent-specific groundwater concentrations were expressed as Hazard Quotients (HQ) and combined into a composite Hazard Index (HI). Predictors included Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, biophysical parameters, and spatiotemporal metrics (2019-2025), alongside soil, climate, hydrology, topography, and land cover. Six supervised classifiers were evaluated using spatially separated test blocks, feature-set ablation, and leave-one-site-out testing. Higher HQ coincided with lower vegetation indices in 24 of 33 metal-site combinations near monitoring wells (sign test p = 0.007). Well HI was negatively correlated with CIRE and canopy chlorophyll content at three sites (Spearman rho as low as -0.71). Random Forest achieved within-site HI classification accuracies of 0.768-0.924 and higher-HI-class recall of 0.965-0.999. For 34 constituent-site combinations, HQ classification accuracies ranged from 0.775 to 0.989. Environmental covariates generally contributed more predictive information than vegetation features. Removing vegetation predictors did not reduce performance, and distance to the CCR unit alone performed best at one site. Zero-shot cross-site accuracy declined to 0.734-0.749, no better than the majority-class baseline. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating satellite observations and environmental data with groundwater measurements for site-calibrated spatial hazard screening. The framework identifies indirect environmental associations rather than directly detecting dissolved metals, highlighting the importance of local calibration and independent validation.

title: Adaptive and Detection-Aware Super-Resolution for Small Object Detection
abstract: Image super-resolution aims to reconstruct a high-resolution image from a low-resolution input and is relevant for surveillance, satellite imagery, medical imaging, and object detection. This paper investigates SRCNN-based single-image super-resolution for a scale factor of x4, starting from a classical baseline and progressively introducing residual learning, Charbonnier loss, and adaptive loss functions. The proposed approach includes a three-region adaptive loss, where image areas are divided into smooth, texture, and edge regions using gradient information. The models are evaluated using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and EdgeMAE in order to measure both reconstruction quality and structural detail preservation. In addition to reconstruction evaluation, the paper analyzes the impact of super-resolution on object detection. A YOLOv8 detector is applied to images processed through bicubic interpolation and SRCNN-based variants, using images from the COCO validation dataset. The results show that improved reconstruction quality does not always lead to better detection performance. However, for small objects, a detection-aware variant combined with residual scaling improves the F1 score compared to the bicubic baseline. These results highlight the importance of task-aware evaluation when super-resolution is used in computer vision pipelines.

title: $ε$-Seg++: Ensembling Across Hierarchy and Training Time for Label-Efficient EM Segmentation
abstract: Semantic segmentation of electron microscopy (EM) volumes is a central step in quantitative cell biology, but dense voxel-wise annotation is prohibitively expensive. $ε$-Seg showed that a hierarchical variational autoencoder trained on sparsely annotated voxels can yield competitive segmentations, but it classifies from its topmost latent level only and operates exclusively on 2D patches. We introduce $ε$-Seg++, which places a semantic expert at every level of the hierarchy and consolidates their predictions with a parameter-free product of experts. We further enable 3D inputs through a leakage-free sub-volume splitting protocol, which allows 2D and 3D models to be compared under identical sparse supervision. Because validation labels are just as scarce as training labels, we treat checkpoint selection as part of the method and average the top-ranked checkpoints, a second ensemble, this time across training time. On the BetaSeg FIB-SEM dataset, the multi-level experts improve 2D mean Dice by about 0.1 at 2,500 training labels. With up to 600 training labels, the 2D model matches or exceeds 3D $ε$-Seg at about one eleventh of its prediction cost. Above roughly a thousand labels, 3D inputs dominate, and at matched annotation cost 3D $ε$-Seg++ reaches a mean Dice of 0.905 versus 0.880 for D3PM, while predicting between 5.4 and 27 times faster (with our checkpoint ensemble or a single model, respectively). Checkpoint ensembling matches single-best selection on average and markedly improves the worst case when the validation set is small.

title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation
abstract: Solar filaments are cool, dense chromospheric plasma structures held by magnetic field lines above polarity inversion lines. Their destabilization triggers coronal mass ejections and severe space weather hazards. Segmenting individual filaments from ground-based GONG H-alpha observations (2048 x 2048 pixels) is challenging due to low contrast, turbulent fibrils, delicate barb structures, and annotator boundary variance. In this technical report, we describe SolarFilNet-V4, a targeted segmentation framework developed for the MAGFiLO 1.0 benchmark (Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026). Our method couples a lightweight Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions (k=15) and dual-frequency feed-forward blocks (DFFN) to follow extended flux ropes while capturing thin central spines. A shallow full-resolution convolutional branch operating at 1024 x 1024 preserves high-frequency edge details and mitigates transformer downsampling. We train the network using multi-task supervision over masks, centerline spines, barb boundaries, and pixel-contrastive representations. At test time, we apply 8-fold dihedral test-time augmentation (D4), bilinearly upscale predictions to the native 2048 x 2048 grid, and apply an activity-adaptive post-processing routine that calibrates morphological joining parameters for quiet versus active solar disks. On the official benchmark, SolarFilNet-V4 achieves an out-of-fold validation Panoptic Quality of 0.4340 and a Public Leaderboard score of 0.380. The model contains 15.46M parameters and requires 224.34 GFLOPs per forward pass, reducing parameter count by 36.8% compared to standard ResNet-34 U-Net baselines.

title: When No-Reference Image Quality Models Meet MAP Estimation in Diffusion Latents
abstract: Contemporary no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) models can effectively quantify perceived image quality, often correlating strongly with human perceptual scores on standard IQA benchmarks. Yet few studies have explored their use as natural image priors for real-world image enhancement and compared them from a perceptual optimization perspective. In this work, we show, for the first time, that NR-IQA models can be plugged into the maximum a posteriori (MAP) framework for image enhancement. Specifically, we perform gradient-based optimization in the diffusion latent space rather than the raw pixel domain, leveraging a pretrained differentiable and bijective diffusion process. Different NR-IQA models yield different enhancement outputs, which facilitate model comparison from a new computational perspective. Guided by rankings obtained under the proposed framework, we develop an improved NR-IQA model by incorporating design elements from other highly ranked methods. Its enhancement outputs are preferred over those of its predecessors while maintaining high image fidelity.

title: Fast Lifelong Clustering via Anchor-based Spectral Embedding
abstract: Clustering has garnered extensive attention owing to its ability to group unlabeled data based on feature similarity. However, most existing methods are developed under the assumption of static data, which severely limits their applicability in large-scale dynamic scenarios. Thus, efficiently clustering large-scale data that arrive continuously has emerged as a challenging problem. In this paper, we propose Fast Lifelong Clustering via Anchor-based Spectral Embedding (FLCASE), an efficient and lightweight framework designed for lifelong clustering. At each time step, FLCASE generates a representative set of anchors and maintains a compact historical memory that accumulates their spectral embedding knowledge. The historical knowledge is leveraged to guide the learning of anchor spectral embeddings for new tasks. Importantly, sample embeddings are learned through a parameter-sharing strategy with anchor embeddings at each step, enabling effective knowledge transfer across tasks. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that FLCASE achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods in both clustering effectiveness and efficiency, thereby providing a practical and scalable solution for lifelong clustering. The code and datasets are available at https://github.com/shutiaocode/FLCASE.

title: CAD-Router: Coupling-Aware Domain Routing via Active Prompt Query for Incremental Multilingual Text Recognition
abstract: Incremental Multilingual Text Recognition (IMLTR) aims to sequentially extend the linguistic capabilities of recognition models while preventing catastrophic forgetting. Prevailing methods adopt a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture where a router assigns images to domain-specific experts but suffer from limited discrimination capabilities in their routing mechanisms. This passive classification paradigm is vulnerable to feature noise and does not establish a clear alignment between visual representations and linguistic domains. To address this challenge, we propose the Coupling-Aware Domain Router (CAD-Router), a novel framework designed to transition the routing mechanism from passive reception to active retrieval. This framework innovatively reconstructs the routing paradigm through two core components. First, the Robust Feature Aggregation (RFA) module introduces a stochastic masking and adaptive weighting mechanism, effectively suppressing noise interference introduced by non-target experts and enhancing the learning process of robust distributed representations. Second, the Domain Prompt Cross-Attention Classification (DPCC) module abandons the traditional MLP-based domain discriminator design and instead adopts a cross-attention mechanism. This module utilizes learnable prompt vectors to actively query corresponding visual prototypes, explicitly coupling linguistic semantics with visual features to achieve proactive matching. Extensive experiments on MLT17 and MLT19 demonstrate that CAD-Router achieves competitive recognition performance across different backbones without additional character-set supervision while effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
