LineEX: Data Extraction from Scientific Line Charts
abstract: In this paper, we introduce LINEEX that extracts data from scientific line charts. We adapt existing vision transformers and pose detection methods and showcase significant performance gains over existing SOTA baselines. We also propose a new loss function and present its effectiveness against existing loss functions. In addition, we synthetically created the largest line chart dataset comprising 430K images. The code is available at https://github.com/Shiva-sankaran/LineEX.

title: Open-Set Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification with Feature Fusion and Vision Transformer
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) is a promising device authentication technique for the Internet of Things (IoT) that leverages hardware impairments to uniquely identify devices. However, most existing RFFI systems operate under a closed-set assumption and lack the ability to detect rogue devices, which poses significant security risks. In this paper, we propose an open-set RFFI approach that jointly performs rogue device detection and legitimate device classification. Specifically, we designed a multi-task RFFI system that integrates an autoencoder (AE) for rogue device detection and a fully connected (FC) layer for classification. To enrich the feature representation, we generated two channel-independent spectrograms (CISs) with distinct window lengths from the I/Q signals, capturing complementary time-frequency characteristics. These CISs were processed in parallel by two Vision Transformer (ViT) networks, and their outputs were fused via feature concatenation to construct a device fingerprint for both tasks. We built a testbed involving ten legitimate LoRa devices and five rogue devices. We conducted a comprehensive experimental evaluation and compared our approach with several benchmark algorithms. Experimental results show that our fused feature multi-task RFFI consistently outperformed the baselines in both legitimate device classification and rogue device detection. Our proposed approach achieved an accuracy of 91.1% and an area under the curve (AUC) of over 0.72 in a realistic wireless scenario where the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was 20 to 30 dB.

title: Adapt, Label, Distill: Foundation-Model Supervision for Efficient Object Detection
abstract: Object detectors often transfer poorly to specialized domains, where box annotations are scarce and deployment requires compact, real-time models. Large vision foundation models can provide offline supervision, but their zero-shot predictions may be poorly aligned with the target domain. We present an adapt-label-distill pipeline that uses limited target annotations to specialize a foundation teacher and transfer its supervision to compact detectors. We adapt SAM3 on the labeled subset, generate pseudo-labels for the remaining unlabeled images, and train YOLOv11 students with confidence-guided supervision. Teacher confidence weights pseudo-label losses, while zero-gating retains uncertain hypotheses during assignment without applying their associated training losses. Experiments across six target domains and three student capacities show substantial gains in several domains, while revealing limited or negative transfer in others. Teacher comparisons under a common hard-label training recipe support the choice of SAM3, and comparisons with an EfficientTeacher adaptation provide additional evidence against an online SSOD baseline. With YOLOv11m, our pipeline improves over STAC-style self-training by up to 15.3 AP and reaches 51.6 AP on Garbage, compared with 54.1 under full supervision. On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the deployed student achieves 188 FPS versus 2.9 FPS for SAM3, benefiting from foundation-model supervision without incurring the teacher's deployment cost. Code is available at https://github.com/zk2172-columbia/ProjectAdaptLabelDistill_ObjectDetection.

title: Spec$^2$R: Recovering Emergent Properties in Supervised Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance across computer vision tasks, but the quality of their learned representations differs drastically depending on the training paradigm. While self-supervised ViTs often demonstrate emergent properties, such as object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, supervised ViTs typically lack these properties, even when trained with strong data augmentations. Understanding the origin of this difference is important for explaining and controlling the object-level structure. To investigate it, we perform a spectral analysis of supervised and self-supervised models, and identify a key distinction: MLP layers in supervised ViTs introduce high-frequency variations into patch representations, disrupting their spatial organization. Motivated by this finding, we propose Spec$^2$R, a lightweight spectral regularization method that fine-tunes the MLP layers of pretrained supervised ViTs. Spec$^2$R recovers object-aligned patch representations and attention maps, while improving adversarial robustness and preserving competitive classification accuracy.

title: Synthetic Augmentation for Data-Scarce Object Detection: Allocation, Dose, and Filtering Across Six Datasets
abstract: Robotic perception for capturing uncooperative orbital objects and inspecting variable industrial products must often operate with limited labelled imagery. We examine a modular synthetic-augmentation pipeline, evaluating generation planning and post-generation filtering as separate interventions, with computational cost as a design constraint. Across six object-detection datasets, FLUX.1-Fill with class-specific LoRA adaptation produced dataset-dependent dose effects; the validation-selected augmentation improved mAP@50:95 on four datasets and reduced it on two. Filtering did not yield consistent gains, and FID, KID, precision, recall, and LPIPS did not consistently track detector changes. The results do not establish that image quality alone identifies useful samples. They motivate standardised evaluation and inexpensive candidate-utility measures that could identify useful samples before detector retraining, reducing repeated training cost.

title: HyMTS: A Multiscale Tensor Factorization-Based Network for Hyperspectral Image Restoration
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) restoration has been explored using deep learning techniques recently. Because hyperspectral images have strong spectral and spatial redundancy, the underlying clean signal is usually represented in a low-dimensional spectral subspace and locally low-rank spatial structures. Existing methods primarily explore dense attention or feature mixing across spectral bands. In this work, we propose HyMTS, a hyperspectral restoration network with a backbone built on the Multi-scale Tensorial Summation (MTS) factorization operator. HyMTS provides a natural architectural mechanism for exploiting a low-rank prior, embedded directly in the network operator rather than imposed via an auxiliary loss or a constraint on the reconstructed output. Specifically, HyMTS stacks a unified block that couples factorized layers with input-adaptive layers, capturing both local and global dependencies across the spectral and spatial dimensions. Extensive experiments without auxiliary data on standard benchmarks for Gaussian and real-noise denoising and single-image super-resolution show that HyMTS efficiently achieves superior or comparable performance to various state-of-the-art approaches.

title: GDD: A Remote Sensing Image Deepfake Detection and Manipulation Localization Dataset
abstract: Verifying image authenticity is a critical need for a variety of applications and decision-making in the remote sensing (RS) domain, yet it is becoming more challenging as advancements in generative AI enable producing increasingly realistic synthetic overhead data. However, existing RS deepfake benchmarks prioritize sheer volume at the expense of visual realism and diversity, while also lacking rigorous out-of-distribution (OOD) testing protocols to evaluate real-world robustness. To address this, we introduce the Geospatial Deepfakes Dataset (GDD), a benchmark for RS deepfake detection and manipulation localization. Rather than relying on uncurated, redundant synthetic generation, GDD comprises images across diverse modern generative models and real image sources, alongside manipulations from diffusion inpainting, splicing, and copy-move operations. Crucially, GDD establishes an OOD evaluation protocol for deepfake detection comprising unseen real image sources and generative models. We benchmark five deepfake detectors and two localization models across intra- and cross-dataset regimes and reveal that detectors trained on high-volume, uncurated benchmarks overfit to dataset-specific artifacts, whereas training on GDD yields superior cross-dataset generalization despite its compact scale. This benchmarking also exposes critical failure modes in current state-of-the-art methods. Combined, GDD and its evaluation protocol establish a high-quality standard for developing and stress-testing detection and localization models in this safety-critical RS domain. The dataset is publicly available.

title: A multimodal foundation model for tissue proteomics and morphology in cancer
abstract: Cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment decisions increasingly rely on integrating tissue morphology with specific molecular readouts of the tumor and its microenvironment. H&E histopathology provides scalable morphology, whereas multiplex spatial proteomics quantifies dozens of proteins in situ with spatial context, but remains selectively deployed, often with different marker panels across cohorts. This creates a translational bottleneck: most patients lack high-depth molecular profiling, and existing models rarely integrate morphology and spatial molecular data in a single framework. We present VirTues-M2, a multimodal foundation model that jointly learns from H&E and spatial proteomics using a novel vision transformer-based architecture. By encoding marker identity during pretraining, VirTues-M2 is robust to missing modalities, imperfect modality pairing or registration, and variable marker panels, enabling unified inference for tissue phenotyping, panoptic cell segmentation, virtual staining, annotation-free biomarker discovery, and reinforcement learning-based adaptive marker panel selection to reduce assay burden. As a concrete demonstration of translational utility, in a newly collected cohort of 1,053 treatment-naive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with paired spatial proteomics and H&E, VirTues-M2 discovers high-risk and low-risk tissue signatures that stratify overall survival in both the discovery cohort and an independent validation cohort, outperforming current state-of-the-art stratification schemes; all enabled by VirTues-M2's ability to jointly analyze both modalities within a single model.

title: Look Where Camouflage Breaks: Concealment-Guided Observation for Camouflaged Object Detection
abstract: A camouflaged object can blend into its surroundings at one scale and become distinguishable at another. Yet a region's apparent ambiguity gives limited guidance on which observation would resolve it. The challenge is to connect the form and scale of concealment to the evidence that a new view can reveal. We introduce CamoBreak, an active framework for camouflaged object detection guided by a Concealment Spectrum. From the image and current predictions, the spectrum measures regional resemblance and boundary ambiguity across comparison scales, distinguishing persistent concealment from separation emerging at finer or broader scales. These measurements guide crop selection from the already-captured image and recognition against global foreground and background references. An object-conditioned spatial preference then selects where local evidence should update the prediction and feature memory, retaining target corrections while suppressing background distractions. Accepted corrections reshape the next measurement, while predicted segmentation benefit determines whether to observe again. Experiments across encoder families and related segmentation tasks show consistent improvements. Targeted analyses support improved small-target recovery, multiple-object coverage, and selective evidence integration. Code will be released.

title: Modern Self-Supervised Vision Transformers Are Pareidolic
abstract: In human perception, pareidolia is the tendency to perceive a meaningful pattern, such as a face, in a random or ambiguous stimulus. We find a similar phenomenon in modern self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs): on white noise, which contains neither objects nor spatial structure, a few directions of their features still form spatially coherent patterns across the patches, imposed by the features themselves. We call this behavior pareidolia, and the span of these directions the pareidolic subspace. On natural images, it holds most of the feature variance in DINOv2 and DINOv3 but little in DINO. This excess explains why DINOv2 and DINOv3, despite stronger dense features, fall far behind DINO in object emergence, the hallmark ability of self-supervised ViTs to identify the patches of an object on their own. Our experiments further show that scaling down their pareidolic subspaces steadily restores their ability to discover objects, so their object emergence is hindered rather than lost. These findings naturally lead to a training-free calibration: Pareidolic Subspace Calibration (PSC) measures the pareidolic subspace only on a noise input and then calibrates the features of natural inputs by scaling its directions down to the variance level of the remaining directions. Across diverse object emergence tasks, PSC improves DINOv2 and DINOv3 by up to 31.7 CorLoc on object discovery, 30.2 maxF on saliency detection and 59.9~$\mathcal{J}$ on video object segmentation. To identify the cause of pareidolia, we trace it block by block and find that it forms in the middle blocks of every self-supervised model we examine but stays strong to the last block only in models trained with a patch-level loss; controlled training confirms that an image-level loss alone lets it fade.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Learning machine learning: Investigating the complementarity and biases of strong gravitational lens finding networks on Euclid data
abstract: The Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) strong lens search presents ECLIPSE, the largest catalogue of strong gravitational lens candidates to date, with >15 000 systems identified across 1900 deg2 of sky. It was constructed using five neural networks applied to approximately 68 million galaxies, followed by citizen science and expert visual inspection. In this work, we compare how the independently developed networks use image information to identify their selection of strong lens candidates. The search combines convolutional neural networks and a vision transformer, using the same pool of data but with different image processing and training choices. We investigate why these networks find different systems and what that means for the completeness of our catalogue. We evaluate all networks on a 50 deg2 calibration set and their application to the full DR1 sample. We find that the networks score candidates very differently, and that combining them recovers over 500 lens candidates within our calibration set at an inspection budget of 2000 objects. On the full DR1 sample, we show that individual networks have distinct biases: some networks favour systems with a larger Einstein radius while others are more sensitive to compact configurations. We also investigate network preferences in terms of lens light profile, mass distribution geometry, photometric redshift, and magnitudes. These findings provide a detailed analysis of how neural network selection biases have shaped the Euclid DR1 ECLIPSE catalogue. The results inform how networks should be combined in future Euclid data releases and upcoming wide-field surveys such as LSST or Roman to maximise both completeness and diversity of the recovered lens population.

title: SRCWDNet: Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network for Multi-Label Remote Sensing Scene Classification
abstract: Multi-label remote sensing scene classification remains a challenging task due to complex spatial-spectral patterns, extreme class imbalance, and inter-label dependencies that are often insufficiently modeled. To address these challenges, we introduce a Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network (SRCWDNet), which integrates three key modules: (1) a Cross-Window Attention module that captures local and global visual context through learnable global tokens; (2) a Dual Label-Graph module that adaptively combines statistical co-occurrence graphs and learned semantic-embedding graphs to facilitate label-relational reasoning; and (3) a Neural Classifier Chain that sequentially predicts labels to exploit inter-label dependencies. Evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and trained with an Asymmetric-Graph-Consistency loss, SRCWDNet achieves accuracies of 98.93% and 96.53%, with corresponding F1-scores of 0.9365 and 0.8723 on the MLRSNet and China-MAS50k datasets, respectively, outperforming CNN, transformer, and lightweight baselines. These findings demonstrate that jointly modeling visual attention and adaptive label correlations can substantially improve multi-label remote sensing scene classification, particularly under long-tailed class distributions.

title: Token Pruning Needs a Protected Sink Token: Coherent Spatial Aggregation in Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are a predominant architecture for computer vision, with token reduction emerging as a popular paradigm to improve their efficiency. Prior work compares reduction algorithms, but not how models respond to them, nor how their response changes with model depth. We propose Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact on the prediction when tokens are explicitly removed during the forward pass. Applying MCTP to recent pretrained models, we observe that most, such as DINOv3, maintain a similar ranking of token importance at every depth (high Coherent Aggregation), while SigLIP 2 does not. This coherence requires predictions to survive pruning, which depends on keeping high-norm "sink" tokens: prefix tokens are kept by design, while prefix-free SigLIP 2 forms them on patch tokens, which pruning may remove. We show that in removing DINOv3's prefix tokens, its predictions and coherence collapse, while protecting only 5 tokens for SigLIP 2 cuts the token impact outside the object's bounding box by up to 62%. Beyond this, MCTP offers a post-hoc method to evaluate how a pretrained ViT responds to pruning, and suggests that token reduction methods should keep "sinks".

title: SIAMBA: A Pseudo-Siamese Mamba-based Deep Learning Network for Multimodal Flood Change Detection
abstract: Flood change detection from bi-temporal multispectral and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is essential for rapid disaster response. In this context, Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery provides discriminative spectral observations, whereas Sentinel-1 SAR provides weather-independent structural information. Using these modalities jointly requires modelling temporal evidence while accounting for cross-modal heterogeneity. In particular, change detection is complicated by cloud contamination, illumination variability, acquisition geometry and speckle, and heterogeneous land-cover responses. To address these challenges, we propose SIAMBA, a pseudo-siamese Mamba-based network for bi-temporal flood change detection from paired Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations. SIAMBA uses dedicated modality-specific encoders with dual-pooling squeeze-and-excitation recalibration and selective state-space processing for long-range spatial context. A gated cross-modal change module derives absolute, signed, and relative log-ratio differences at multiple semantic levels, and attention-refined skip connections support progressive multi-scale decoding. Experiments are carried out on OMBRIA benchmark, which includes an independent test set and geographically diverse subsets in France, Albania, Guyana, and Timor. SIAMBA achieves 81.98% IoU, and 93.57% OA on the independent test set, reaching the highest values in the considered comparison. It also provides the highest unweighted average IoU and OA across four regional subsets spatially disjuncted. These results indicate that combining selective state-space contextual modelling with gated multiscale discrepancy learning effectively improves flood change mapping across the evaluated geographic settings.

title: How Do Deep Networks Encode and Selectively Use Information? Shared Encoding and Conditional Signed Readout in Vision and Language Models
abstract: How can trained deep networks retain contextual information across internal representations while using it selectively in a decision? We study this question through controlled background-texture edits in vision classifiers and entity-binding edits in frozen language models. Across both modalities, factor perturbations preserve recognizable structure across pre-fixed, mutually disjoint blocks of hidden units: visual channel blocks match their complements more closely for the same image than for other images under the same texture edit, while language blocks transfer a relational direction fitted under one query role to rank relational states within held-out name pairs under the other role. We then decompose the local output change into signed channel and pathway contributions. In a convolutional classifier, net channel-level reinforcement ($R^{(512)}>1$) coexists on individual images with cancellation between positive- and negative-weight groups ($R^{(2)}<1$). Holding weights, the paired relation edit, and red/blue answer words fixed, switching prompt presentation reverses the mean finite selection effect in Qwen2.5. Two held-out tests validate this mechanism. Attenuating development-selected antagonistic units amplifies edit effects on unseen inputs; in a vision transformer, attenuating the same frozen units in one forward pass increases the mean magnitude of the background-edit effect on one class margin and reduces it on another, with the opposite pattern for a second group (four-cell paired interaction $+78.30\times 10^{-5}$ logit). Finally, combining conditional channel variance with fixed downstream readout weights predicts single-channel pruning recovery across ten cuts. These results show how shared encoding and conditional signed readout can coexist in vision and language models.

title: GRAIN: Shared-Budget Complementary Re-observation for Object Detection
abstract: Re-running a frozen detector on enlarged image crops recovers small and crowded objects without retraining, yet every crop costs an extra detector call. Existing slicing and adaptive-cropping pipelines plan crops per image in isolation, even though inspection demand varies widely across an image collection. We present GRAIN, which unifies cross-image call allocation and bounded-output admission around cross-image comparable resolution-closure gains over boundary-safe crop interiors. Coarse hypotheses carry resolution deficits, crops close a geometric share of those deficits for hypotheses enclosed in their interior positive region, and multiplicative residuals discount covered evidence within a monotone submodular surrogate. Prefix sums and a global max-heap execute this collection-wide plan on CPU before crop inference, and Positive-Region Fusion aligns post-inference spatial admission with the planned interior support before class-balanced top- selection. Across 17 frozen detectors from five families on COCO, CrowdHuman, and VisDrone-DET, GRAIN beats call-matched tiling in 100 of 102 AP@100 settings and transfers to AI-TOD-v2. With RF-DETR-S on CrowdHuman, it nearly matches two-crop tiling using one eighth of the crop calls. At fixed budgets, the surrogate orders candidate plans with Spearman correlations of 0.95 to 0.99 while the sweep attains at least 98% of the exact surrogate optimum. Code will be publicly released.

title: Sequential Monitoring of Image Streams Using Energy Statistics
abstract: Sequential monitoring of image data is a high-velocity, high-dimensional big data problem in statistics and machine learning, with wide applications in manufacturing industries, satellite imaging, medical diagnostics, and remote sensing. This is a challenging task because image intensity functions are often contaminated by noise and contain discontinuities and other complicated spatial structures. In the literature, a vast majority of image-monitoring methods rely on changes in image intensity values to detect out-of-control images. However, such approaches are often unreasonable in applications where insignificant changes in image contrast or background intensity should not indicate an out-of-control image as long as the boundaries of the image objects remain unchanged. In this article, we propose a nonparametric Phase II image-monitoring procedure based on energy distance that directly monitors changes in the distribution of image boundaries. The proposed method constructs a moving-window energy-distance-based control statistic by comparing the distribution of recently observed image boundaries with that of a fixed in-control reference sample. The central idea behind the proposed boundary-based approach is twofold: first, to reduce the dimensionality of high-resolution images by retaining relevant edge information, and second, to provide a robust monitoring procedure that is less sensitive to insignificant smooth changes in image intensity. The proposed construction offers a computationally efficient distributional approach to image monitoring without requiring a parametric model for out-of-control images. Theoretical justifications and superior performance in numerical comparisons ensure that the proposed control chart can be useful to many researchers and practitioners.

title: GSDet: Gaussian Splatting for Oriented Object Detection
abstract: Oriented object detection has advanced with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers. However, modern detectors still rely on predefined object candidates, such as anchors in CNN-based methods or queries in transformer-based methods, which struggle to capture spatial information effectively. To address the limitations, we propose GSDet, a novel framework that formulates oriented object detection as Gaussian splatting. Specifically, our approach performs detection within a 3D feature space constructed from image features, where 3D Gaussians are employed to represent oriented objects. These 3D Gaussians are projected onto the image plane to form 2D Gaussians, which are then transformed into oriented boxes. Furthermore, we optimize the mean, anisotropic covariance, and confidence scores of these randomly initialized 3D Gaussians, using a decoder that incorporates 3D Gaussian sampling. Moreover, our method exhibits flexibility, enabling adaptive control and a dynamic number of Gaussians during inference. Experiments on 3 datasets indicate that GSDet achieves AP$_{50}$ gains of 0.7\% on DIOR-R, 0.3\% on DOTA-v1.0, and 0.55\% on DOTA-v1.5 when evaluated with adaptive control and outperforms mainstream detectors.

title: ReDiffDet: Rotation-equivariant Diffusion Model for Oriented Object Detection
abstract: The diffusion model has been successfully applied to various detection tasks. However, it still faces several challenges when used for oriented object detection: objects that are arbitrarily rotated require the diffusion model to encode their orientation information; uncontrollable random boxes inaccurately locate objects with dense arrangements and extreme aspect ratios; oriented boxes result in the misalignment between them and image features. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReDiffDet, a framework that formulates oriented object detection as a rotation-equivariant denoising diffusion process. First, we represent an oriented box as a 2D Gaussian distribution, forming the basis of the denoising paradigm. The reverse process can be proven to be rotation-equivariant within this representation and model framework. Second, we design a conditional encoder with conditional boxes to prevent boxes from being randomly placed across the entire image. Third, we propose an aligned decoder for alignment between oriented boxes and image features. The extensive experiments demonstrate ReDiffDet achieves promising performance and significantly outperforms the diffusion model baseline.

title: Assembly-JEPA: Using World Models for Fine-Grained Industrial Image Verification
abstract: Automated verification of industrial assembly processes remains a challenging problem due to substantial visual variability, limited availability of labeled defect data, and the fine-grained nature of many assembly errors. Existing approaches often rely on object detection, CAD models, or supervised classification pipelines, which can struggle to generalize across changing products and assembly configurations. In this work, we propose a novel self-supervised assembly verification framework based on Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs). Starting from the JEPA-based world model LeWorldModel, we investigate how the architecture must be adapted to verify the correctness of fine-grained assembly operations. To this end, we formulate assembly verification as a predictive world modeling task operating on before-and-after observations of assembly processes. Experimental results on industrial assembly tasks demonstrate that the proposed approach reliably detects both fine-grained incorrect assembly states and action-state mismatches, achieving an AUROC of 86.9% on a newly introduced assembly verification dataset. These results indicate that JEPA-based predictive representations constitute a promising foundation for robust and data-efficient industrial assembly verification.

title: Field-Level Crop Classification via Similarity-Induced Supervision from Imperfect Labels
abstract: Regional-scale crop mapping is critical for food production monitoring, yet remains challenging in tropical regions, where persistent cloud cover limits optical imagery. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enables continuous observation throughout the agricultural cycle, but a second obstacle is label quality: national-scale land cover products exhibit systematic biases that underestimate less prevalent crops, and training directly on them inherits and amplifies their errors. This work proposes a methodology to build large-scale crop classification models from imperfect public land cover products, requiring no new field campaign, ground survey, or manual label correction. The approach combines two mechanisms. The first reduces the semantic inconsistency of the labels by shifting supervision from the sample level to the group level: a similarity-based clustering model organizes SAR time series into coherent groups, and noisy labels are used only to assign each group its most representative class. The resulting clusters are highly pure with respect to the reference classes (89.0% and 91.2% in the two study regions). The second reduces the spatial inconsistency of the predictions: a segmentation model delineates crop field boundaries from optical imagery, and patch-level predictions are consolidated by majority voting within each field, yielding spatially coherent maps. Evaluated in two Brazilian municipalities, Campo Verde (Mato Grosso) and Luís Eduardo Magalhães (Bahia), the approach consistently outperforms the noisy baseline in mean class accuracy, with gains of up to 10.14 percentage points, especially for minority crops. A state-scale analysis across Mato Grosso and Bahia shows stable behavior without further model adjustment, and the derived municipal crop areas are consistent with official IBGE/PAM statistics, an independent estimate the model never observes.

title: AXE: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report
abstract: This report presents a comprehensive pipeline for developing an end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving model for the Physical AI AV Track. The framework consists of data curation, HD map auto-labelling, data-driven imitation learning, and simulator-based reinforcement learning. To ensure safety in the closed-loop setting, we introduce a selection-based E2E planning approach that leverages object detection and BEV segmentation to filter out trajectory candidates likely to cause collisions or off-road driving. Trained on NVIDIA NuRec and the NVIDIA PAI-AV dataset, our method scores a fixed vocabulary of trajectory candidates for collision, drivable-area compliance, and progress learned from simulated rollouts, and selects the best candidate that passes the filter. This design highlights the effectiveness of combining E2E planning with perception-based trajectory filtering for safe and reliable closed-loop autonomous driving.

title: Struct2Det: Grounding Category Structure in Visual Evidence for Few-Shot Object Detection
abstract: Few-shot detectors struggle to distinguish categories that look alike but differ in local components, because a few examples rarely reveal which differences determine category identity. Category descriptions specify components and relations but do not establish their presence in an image. We propose Struct2Det, which uses category structure to guide detection and verify candidates in three stages. Relational Structure Encoding maps category graphs to component embeddings and a global condition. Component-Grounded Detection uses component queries to retrieve multi-scale image evidence that, with the global condition, modulates category text embeddings for initial detection. Verification-Guided Refinement matches candidate regions with components expected by their top-scoring categories; when class scores are close and matches are reliable, matched pairs correct region features before the shared detector predicts again. Category structure informs both classification inputs: text embeddings integrate image-wide component evidence, while region features incorporate candidate-specific matches. We also construct InduSym, with 88,912 symbol instances across 275 categories from 674 engineering drawings and a structural graph per category. Struct2Det improves few-shot-category AP over the strongest baseline by 6.02 points on InduSym and 9.68 on Digitize-PID, with the highest base-category AP on both. InduSym ablations show few-shot gains from correct category structure, image-level retrieval, and candidate verification. Further tests show gains in few-shot natural-object detection and zero-shot Chinese character recognition.

title: Cross-calibration of Hera/HyperScout-H with MRO/CRISM and MEx/OMEGA based on Mars observations
abstract: On March 12, 2025, Hera, the European Space Agency's planetary defense mission, performed a Mars flyby en route to the asteroid system (65803) Didymos-Dimorphos. During this event, HyperScout-H (HS-H), the spacecraft's hyperspectral imager, acquired five high spatial resolution images over the southern hemisphere of Mars. These observations provide an opportunity for systematic cross-calibration of HS-H with two established Mars orbital instruments, Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) on board the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (Murchie et al., 2007), and Observatoire pour la Minéralogie, l'Eau, les Glaces et l'Activité (OMEGA) on board Mars Express (Bibring et al., 2004). This study evaluates the performance, reliability, and readiness of HS-H for the forthcoming asteroid observation phase by comparing it with CRISM and OMEGA data. We selected 21 surface regions spanning diverse terrain types from three HS-H images in which the Martian surface fills the entire field of view. These images were corrected, calibrated, and co-registered to associate each pixel with latitude and longitude. The relative inter-channel correction factors are close to unity for bands 3-25 (0.688-0.952 μm), with standard deviations of 0.52% for OMEGA and 0.62% for CRISM, indicating good agreement in spectral shape. Bands 1 and 2 show a systematic mismatch of 4.7% and 3.6%. The absolute flux correction factors reveal offsets of 8% relative to OMEGA and approximately 0.7% relative to CRISM, with mean inter-image standard deviations below 2%. These results confirm the radiometric stability of HS-H and establish a calibration framework for future Didymos-Dimorphos observations.

title: Delineate anything flow: fast, country-level field boundary detection from any source
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Accurate satellite data-based field boundary delineation is essential for land management and agricultural statistics, but integrating tile-level predictions into continuous large-area vector products introduces topological errors and computational challenges. We present Delineate Anything Flow (DelAnyFlow), a framework for scalable field instance mapping that integrates the YOLOv11-based DelAny model with structured post-processing, cross-tile instance unification, vectorization, and topology-consistent simplification. DelAny is trained on the Field Boundary Instance Segmentation-22 M (FBIS-22M) dataset, containing 672,909 multi-resolution patches from 0.25 to 10 m and 22.9 million field instances. It achieves the mean average precision with the intersection over union (IoU) threshold set at 0.5 (mAP@0.5) of 0.720 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.477, while providing substantially faster inference than the zero-shot segment anything model (SAM2). Component-level evaluation shows that cross-tile unification reduces seam-induced field fragmentation by a factor of 4–6, while anchor-guided simplification reduces separated neighbouring fields from about 20% to 0.2% at comparable geometric compression. Demonstrating operational scalability, DelAnyFlow mapped Ukraine’s entire 603,000 km2 territory in 5.4 h on a single workstation. Quantitative comparisons with independent operational products show larger IoU values and small-object recall (producer accuracy), particularly for fragmented agricultural landscapes; DelAnyFlow reaches an IoU of 0.971 and a small-object recall of 0.878, compared with 0.926 and 0.405 for the best operational product. The framework therefore provides a reproducible pathway from tile-level GeoAI predictions to spatially continuous, topologically consistent field-boundary products at regional and national scales. Code, models, the dataset, and national vectors are available at https://lavreniuk.github.io/Delineate-Anything/ .

title: Monte Carlo biphasic estimation of fire properties (McBEF): Part I, algorithm formulation
abstract: Sub-pixel fire characterization is essential for quantifying wildfire energetics, combustion phase dynamics, and their atmospheric impacts from satellite observations. This study presents a series of Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) to systematically evaluate the influence of temperature phase complexity, channel selection, and intra-phase temperature heterogeneity on the performance of a Bayesian retrieval framework. Using synthetic observations derived from a multi-phase radiance model, we assess retrieval skill across key fire properties—including Fire Radiative Power (FRP), visible energy fraction (VEF), and flaming heat flux—under realistic sensor constraints. Results show that a bi-phasic fire model provides a strong balance between accuracy and observational feasibility, outperforming conventional approaches such as Wooster’s FRP regression, particularly in low-intensity fire scenarios. FRP is the retrieved quantity most resilient to model and observational uncertainties, while VEF and heat flux estimates are more sensitive to both fire phase partitioning and spectral coverage. Shortwave and mid-infrared bands, especially the day–night band (DNB) and 2.25 μ m channels, are shown to offer the greatest constraint on retrieval accuracy. We further analyze the impact of intra-phase temperature variability and propose practical filtering strategies for identifying low-confidence cases, such as smoldering-dominated fires. The theoretical framework is applicable to multi-channel fire observations more generally, while its companion Part II implementation focuses specifically on nighttime VIIRS observations.

title: Multi-angular remote sensing-derived directional fractional vegetation cover for improved C-factor estimation in RUSLE modeling
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The cover and management factor ( C -factor) is a crucial parameter influencing the accuracy of soil erosion model estimates. However, conventional approaches often overlook the influence of vegetation vertical structure, particularly understory vegetation, which may lead to biased estimation of erosion severity. To address this issue, a synergistic C -factor estimation framework was developed that integrates multi-angular remote sensing (RS) observations and directional fractional vegetation cover ( DFVC ) to enhance the characterization of vegetation structure and improve C -factor estimation accuracy. The PROSAIL model was used to simulate canopy reflectance under different viewing angles, from which a dataset of multi-angular vegetation indices (VIs) was constructed. Among these VIs, the index most strongly correlated with leaf area index ( LAI ) was selected to develop a progressive “VIs– LAI – DFVC – C -factor” estimation model. The applicability of the method was further evaluated using field measurements collected across different vegetation types and structural conditions. The perpendicular vegetation index ( PVI ) was found to be significantly correlated with LAI and was identified as the optimal feature for LAI retrieval. Among the multi-angular combinations, the three-angle combination of 0°, 36°, and 55° was retained for LAI retrieval and achieved an RMSE of 0.233 and a MAPE of 0.059. Based on the overall evaluation, the 0° + 36° configuration was adopted for final DFVC -based C -factor mapping. The proposed estimation framework demonstrated high reliability ( R 2 = 0.754), with a mean C -factor estimate value of 0.019 in the study area. This study highlights the importance of incorporating vegetation vertical structure information in C -factor estimation and demonstrates that multi-angular RS can offer effective complementary information for characterizing structural features such as canopy gaps and directional occlusion. The proposed framework presents a new approach for quantitative soil erosion monitoring and environmental management.

title: Sound2Vision: Generating Diverse Visuals from Audio through Cross-Modal Latent Alignment
abstract: How does audio describe the world around us? In this work, we propose a method for generating images of visual scenes from diverse in-the-wild sounds. This cross-modal generation task is challenging due to the significant information gap between auditory and visual signals. We address this challenge by designing a model that aligns audio-visual modalities by enriching audio features with visual information and translating them into the visual latent space. These features are then fed into the pre-trained image generator to produce images. To enhance image quality, we use sound source localization to select audio-visual pairs with strong cross-modal correlations. Our method achieves substantially better results on the VEGAS and VGGSound datasets compared to previous work and demonstrates control over the generation process through simple manipulations to the input waveform or latent space. Furthermore, we analyze the geometric properties of the learned embedding space and demonstrate that our learning approach effectively aligns audio-visual signals for cross-modal generation. Based on this analysis, we show that our method is agnostic to specific design choices, showing its generalizability by integrating various model architectures and different types of audio-visual data.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Task-Aware Transformer for Video Procedure Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Procedure learning aims to jointly recognize and localize key steps from instructional videos given an ordered step list. The goal is to predict precise temporal spans for each step. Existing methods typically treat this as a sequence-to-sequence alignment task. However, as the provided step lists lack deeper task-level knowledge, we observe that these models often struggle with two challenges: (1) Missing cross-route task generalization, where models overfit to single annotated pattern and fail to capture the diverse yet semantically valid routes of the same task; and (2) Insufficient temporal-visual grounding, where the absence of concrete timing and appearance priors in the provided step lists leads to boundary drift and step error when predicting on individual videos. To address these challenges, we propose the Task-Aware Transformer (TAT), a unified framework that integrates task-level priors into the alignment process. TAT consists of two complementary components: (i) Task-Aware Structured Memory Construction, which aggregates semantic, temporal, and visual knowledge from multiple execution routes into a structured memory. To ensure the memory remains faithful to supervision, we introduce a Memory Constraint Loss that jointly encodes semantic consistency and temporal order. (ii) Retrieval-Augmented Video-Step Alignment, which retrieves a knowledge-enriched route from the memory to serve as contextual guidance, injecting fine-grained priors into the frame-to-step alignment. We further design two alignment strategies, a lightweight cross-modal decoder and a Vision-Language Model association, to balance efficiency and generalization. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks (YouCookII, COIN, CrossTask, and ProceL) demonstrate that TAT consistently outperforms existing methods, particularly in generalizing to novel procedural compositions, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Learning Physical Priors Embedded in Underwater Imaging and Light Attenuation for Self-Supervised Underwater Depth Estimation
abstract: Depth information is crucial for the perception and navigation of underwater robots. While existing methods incorporate underwater physical priors into self-supervised monocular depth estimation to mitigate the impact of image degradation, challenges such as depth misestimation in background regions, loss of edge details, and limited generalization capabilities remain to be addressed. In this paper, we propose UIEMono, which transforms the physical characteristics of underwater imaging and light propagation into depth estimation cues and incorporates them into the self-supervised learning pipeline. Specifically, multiple networks predict the latent components of the underwater image formation model to reconstruct the input image. This reconstruction process, combined with the geometric projection relationships between adjacent frames, assists the network in learning to infer scene depth. During training, we adopt two distinct estimation strategies for the forward attenuation coefficient: in the early stages, it is predicted as a global constant within each image to ensure training stability; in the later stages, a two-term exponential model is utilized to model its dependency on depth, thereby achieving joint optimization. The constraint relationship between the latent components of homologous images is used to provide additional supervision. We leverage the inherent relationship between depth and light attenuation to provide additional cues for guiding network learning. Furthermore, we weight the reprojection loss based on the intensity differences between channels to avoid the negative impact of photometric errors in background regions. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance and can generalize to a wider range of underwater scenarios.

title: DC-SQEM: Medial Mesh Extraction by Dual Contouring with Spherical Quadric Error Metric
abstract: The medial axis, as a compact representation, describes not only the boundary but also the interior of the shape, and has been widely used in analyzing and simplifying shapes. However, approximating feature-preserving medial axis from unstructured data, such as oriented point clouds, remains challenging due to the lack of explicit connectivity and the presence of noise in the source. We propose DC-SQEM, a dual-contouring-based framework that computes medial meshes (an explicit representation of the medial axis) directly from oriented point clouds without relying on watertight manifold surfaces or volumetric structures. With the help of an adaptive octree, our method fits local medial spheres for each cell based on the Spherical Quadric Error Metric (SQEM). We address several long-standing robustness issues in dual-contouring and mesh extraction, including out-of-cell solutions, unstable feature classification, and redundant topological connections. To this end, we introduce virtual nodes, a feature-downgrading strategy, and a geometry-driven topology-aware cleanup procedure, enabling robust SQEM-based medial dual contouring with clean mesh outputs. Unlike prior point-cloud-based methods that produce either only 1D skeletal structures or incomplete medial features, our method preserves sharp geometric features from the input and reconstructs a complete medial structure, including sheets, curves, seams, and junctions. Compared to restricted-power-diagram-based approaches, our algorithm can handle point clouds as input, without having a strong requirement on water-tightness or manifoldness.

title: Revisiting out-of-distribution detection in semantic difference space
SepsisAgent: Multi-agent multimodal clinical reasoning for sepsis
Multi-scale implicit neural representation learning for low-dose CT image denoising
Regional-scale field-level estimation and mapping of tillage practices in areas with crop diversity
abstract: The imperative for sustainable agriculture has led to the promotion of conservation tillage practices, which are critical for maintaining soil health and reducing negative environmental impacts. However, the ability to verify the adoption of these practices at a regional scale and with minimal costs remains a challenge, particularly in regions with diverse crop systems. This study presents a satellite-imagery-based random forest classifier that integrates crop class information and a customized importance weighting technique for field-level, regional-scale mapping of tillage practices in crop-diverse regions. We use eastern Washington State, U.S., with multiple grains, legumes, and canola as a case study. Using 577 field-level ground-truth data points across two counties, the tillage classifier achieved a median overall accuracy of 84%, representing a 15 percentage point improvement over the baseline median overall accuracy of 69%, driven by the inclusion of crop class and the application of importance weighting. Specific crop classes, including grains, legumes, and canola, showed accuracy improvements of 6, 42, and 13 percentage points, respectively. While the model showed promising results, limitations such as overprediction of no-tillage in non-grain crop classes were identified, pointing to the need for further refinement with additional data. The model was applied to map tillage practices across dryland fields in eastern Washington State for the years 2012, 2017, and 2022, and the predictions were generally congruent with the USDA Census of Agriculture county-level statistics. This research offers a scalable tool for the verification of conservation tillage practice adoption, supporting both regional and global monitoring efforts for sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Human–AI Divergence in Ego-Centric Action Recognition Under Spatial and Spatiotemporal Manipulations
abstract: Humans consistently outperform state-of-the-art AI models in action recognition, particularly in challenging real-world conditions involving low resolution, occlusion, and visual clutter.e those utilised by humans Understanding the sources of this performance gap is essential for developing more robust and human-aligned models. In this paper, we present a large-scale human AI comparative study of egocentric action recognition using human-defined Minimal Identifiable Recognition Crops (MIRCs), defined as the smallest spatial or spatiotemporal regions sufficient for reliable human recognition. We used our previously introduced, Epic-ReduAct, a systematically spatially reduced and temporally scrambled dataset derived from 36 EPIC-KITCHENS videos, spanning multiple spatial reduction levels and temporal conditions. Recognition performance is evaluated using over 3,000 human participants, Side4Video, and Qwen 3.5 9B models. Our analysis combines quantitative metrics, Average Reduction Rate and Recognition Gap, with qualitative analyses of spatial (high-, mid-, and low-level visual features) and spatiotemporal factors, including a categorisation of actions into Low Temporal Actions (LTA) and High Temporal Actions (HTA). Results show that human performance exhibits sharp declines when transitioning from MIRCs to sub-MIRCs, reflecting a strong reliance on sparse, semantically critical cues such as hand object interactions. In contrast, the model degrades more gradually and often relies on contextual and mid- to low-level features, sometimes even exhibiting increased confidence under spatial reduction. Temporally, humans remain robust to scrambling when key spatial cues are preserved, whereas the model often shows insensitivity to temporal disruption, revealing class-dependent temporal sensitivities. Overall, our findings demonstrate that strong benchmark performance can obscure fundamental human AI misalignment and highlight limitations in current spatial and spatiotemporal representations, suggesting concrete directions for more efficient and human-aligned action recognition systems.

title: GRAIL: Granularity Adaptive Representation for Class-Incremental Learning with Granular-Ball
APEX: Exploiting Anatomical and Pathological Insights for Context-Aware Gaze Estimation
Disentanglement-Guided Multi-Teacher Relational Distillation for Federated Class-Incremental Facial Expression Recognition
abstract: Conventional facial expression recognition (FER) methods often train the model on large-scale centralized expression data. However, expression data are often distributed across heterogeneous devices and incrementally collected in practice. In this paper, we study a little-studied yet important task named federated class-incremental FER (FCI-FER), which aims to incrementally identify unseen compound expressions with the model initially trained on easily accessible basic expressions under the federated learning settings. To address the unique problems of catastrophic forgetting and heterogeneous disturbances across clients in FCI-FER, we propose a disentanglement-guided multi-teacher relational distillation (DMT-RD) method which follows a novel "distillation and disentanglement" paradigm. For local training, we design a multi-teacher hypergraph relational distillation (MTD) module to capture semantic relations between expressions and learn expression features. Meanwhile, we develop a disturbance encoding (DE) module to learn client-specific disturbance information. By minimizing the mutual information (MI) loss between the outputs of the MTD and DE modules, we can achieve feature disentanglement and reduce the negative influence of specific disturbances on local training. For global training, we introduce a multi-teacher learning strategy by clustering historical clients to comprehensively capture client diversity across communication rounds. Our method can effectively preserve old knowledge while learning new compound expressions under federated settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method against several state-of-the-art federated class-incremental learning methods on benchmark datasets.

title: FuseSR+: Spatial-Temporal Fusion for High-Scale Super-Resolution
abstract: The workload of real-time rendering is steeply increasing as the demand for high resolution, high refresh rates, and high realism rises, overwhelming most graphics cards. To mitigate this problem, one of the most popular solutions is to render images at a lower resolution to reduce rendering overhead and then manage to accurately upsample the low-resolution (LR) rendered image to the high-resolution (HR) results, a.k.a. super-resolution techniques. Theoretically, reconstructing a higher-resolution image requires integrating additional information beyond the rendered low-resolution image. Most existing methods predominantly rely on temporal information from low-resolution sources, such as historical frames. However, the temporal information accumulated frame-by-frame is generally too sparse to recover the fine details for high-scale super-resolution. To break the limit, this paper proposes an efficient and effective neural super-resolution method that utilizes non-aligned spatial and temporal information to achieve stable large-scale super-resolution. We introduce low-cost historical and current high-resolution auxiliary G-buffers as additional cues to enhance high-frequency detail reconstruction, spatial coherence, and temporal stability. To efficiently align and fuse various features — including spatial and temporal, low- and high-resolution features — under runtime constraints, we propose several novel technical modules, specifically, an H-Net architecture, a corresponding pixel shuffling and unshuffling layers for aligning low- and high-resolution features in a compact network, and a lightweight temporal feature recurrent module for aggregating HR temporal features. These techniques significantly reduce rendering overhead without noticeable quality deterioration. Experiments demonstrate that our method is able to produce temporally consistent reconstructions in both 4 × 4 and the more challenging 8 × 8 large-scale upsampling tasks at 4K resolution with real-time performance, while delivering substantially improved visual quality, significant performance gains, and remarkable temporal stability compared to existing methods.

title: Satellite embedding‑based mapping of grassland mowing frequency and its response to drought in Denmark
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Mowing frequency is a primary indicator of grassland management intensity, forage productivity, and biogeochemical dynamics. Yet, despite a growing body of literature, operational frameworks capable of mapping cutting regimes at a regional scale remain computationally demanding and lack independent benchmarking. Here, we evaluate the potential of Google AlphaEarth annual satellite embeddings to map grassland mowing frequency across Denmark (2017–2023) at 10-m resolution. Using farmer logs across multiple years (n = 346), Random Forest emerged as the top-performing classifier, achieving an overall accuracy of 0.73 and a macro F1-score of 0.65. Our workflow substantially outperformed the operational Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) Grassland Mowing Events (GRAME) benchmark (overall accuracy of 0.24). Latent embedding dimensions strongly correlated with macro-climatic and vegetation drivers (|ρ| > 0.8). Once deployed across the full nation extent, under 6 min of computing time, the model predictions proved ecologically consistent across pedological and agronomic gradients. We further applied Dirichlet regression to quantify how hydrological drought, indexed by a 6-month scale Standardised Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI-6), affects national mowing patterns. The extreme 2018 drought triggered a landscape-wide management de-intensification, shifting the intensive (≥4 cuts) regime into a 2 cuts system. During moderate droughts, regional responses diverged sharply: western regions exhibited agronomic resilience, whereas drier eastern islands repeatedly reverted to lower-intensity management. These results demonstrate that satellite foundation models can underpin scalable, automated agronomic monitoring and reveal grassland management’s acute sensitivity to drought, insights essential for adaptive land-use planning and national-scale environmental reporting.

title: Mapping small water bodies and their dynamics with deep learning: fusion of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery at semi-monthly 10 m spatial resolution
abstract: Mapping small water body (SWB) dynamics at high spatiotemporal resolution remains challenging because optical imagery is frequently obscured by clouds, whereas SAR imagery is affected by speckle noise and blurred boundaries. Existing Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 fusion methods often have limited capability in fully exploiting the complementary information of the two sensors, leading to uncertainties in SWB mapping. Here we propose a deep learning-based method, the multiscale global-local water feature fusion network (MGLWNet), to map semi-monthly SWB dynamics via deep fusion of time-series Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery. A large-scale dataset containing 1,193,347 SWBs (<10 ha) was constructed. MGLWNet incorporates a cloud detection branch to improve feature discrimination under cloud-contaminated conditions and a multiscale global-local feature module that combines atrous spatial pyramid pooling and multi-scale self-attention to capture both fine spatial details and global contextual information. When tested on cloud-free and cloud-contaminated datasets, MGLWNet outperformed Random Forest and several state-of-the-art deep learning models. Compared with Sentinel-1-based surface water mapping, the proposed fusion strategy substantially reduced commission errors, while the cloud detection branch effectively decreased omission errors in cloudy regions. MGLWNet was applied to map semi-monthly 10 m surface water dynamics in high-density SWB areas of Hubei Province (185,900 km2) over the period 2017–2024. Unbiased accuracy estimates were performed for validation. The semi-monthly surface water maps have a producer's accuracy of 87.65% (±2.50%) and user's accuracy of 93.11% (±2.62%), respectively, with a 95% confidence interval. Compared with Landsat-based products, the method captured more frequent intra-monthly SWB variations and detected more long-term changes (e.g. the appearance and disappearance of small ponds). The resulting high-temporal-resolution dataset further enabled characterization of multiple SWB change types, including stable seasonal water, water gain, water loss, dry periods, and wet periods. This study highlights the importance of deep learning and image fusion for characterizing spatiotemporal continuous SWB dynamics.

title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

title: Bridging the Thermal Gap: Data-Model Collaborative Transfer for Infrared Perception
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Infrared visual perception fundamentally differs from visible-domain vision due to its distinct thermal imaging mechanism and varying imaging conditions. Existing methods typically decouple data construction from model transfer, overlooking their interdependence: model accuracy and robustness depend critically on the coverage and composition of training observations, while effective model transfer requires explicit modeling of infrared-specific imaging characteristics. To address this issue, we propose a data-model collaborative transfer framework for infrared visual perception. At the data level, a task-responsive generator learns weights over a feasible infrared imaging-variation space to construct informative training observations. At the model level, a formation-guided representation module derives complementary radiance-structure and response-detail descriptors from infrared observations. We further design a thermal-aware adapter that uses these descriptors to modulate intermediate representations and produce lightweight residual corrections for model transfer. A single-loop training strategy coordinates data generation, representation learning, and adapter optimization without expensive nested optimization. Extensive experiments on image enhancement, depth estimation, small-target detection, and semantic segmentation demonstrate consistent performance improvements across multiple foundation-model backbones with a small trainable parameter budget.

title: Real-World Spectral Compressive Imaging by Learning a Physics-Informed Forward Model
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Coded aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI) enables snapshot acquisition of hyperspectral image (HSI) by compressing a three-dimensional spectral data into a single two-dimensional measurement. While recent learning-based reconstruction methods achieve impressive performance on simulated datasets, their performance often degrades significantly on real CASSI systems, revealing a simulation-to-reality gap. This gap arises from a mismatch between the complex real imaging process and the reconstruction mappings learned from idealized simulated data. To bridge this simulation-to-reality gap, we propose a learnable physics-informed forward model (LPFM) that incorporates the physical structure of CASSI into a learnable proxy network to model the complex real imaging process. To train the LPFM, we construct the first real-world spectral compressive imaging (rSCI) dataset. The rSCI dataset contains 219 pairs of static HSI-CASSI images across diverse indoor and outdoor scenes, as well as additional dynamic CASSI videos. Leveraging rSCI and LPFM, we establish the first real-world benchmark for CASSI reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that incorporating data generated by LPFM effectively reduces the simulation-to-reality gap and consistently improves reconstruction performance across various state-of-the-art methods.

title: Knowledge-enhanced Incomplete Multi-view Clustering on Relational Knowledge
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC) methods have drawn increasingly attention these years, as their better potential to the complex real-world scenario. The key of the models in such tasks is how to perform high-quality imputation. Traditional intra-view and inter-view imputation strategies rely mainly on observed features. Such strategies may introduce semantic noise and biased estimations, making it difficult to recover the true semantics of missing views. Meanwhile, they are hard to directly apply to relational knowledge MVC, as fail to utilize the knowledge sufficiently. To this end, we propose a simple yet effective knowledge-enhanced anchor-based IMVC framework with two specific knowledge enhancement mechanisms, i.e., one for anchors, and the other for anchor graph. With the structural knowledge enhancement, the model can be gifted with better expressive ability and get good results. Extensive experiments compared with 10 models have proven the promising capacity of our method from 5 aspects, i.e., superiority, stability, sensitivity, complexity, and visualization. Notably, as the first work on IMVC on relational knowledge, 45 incomplete multi-view datasets are constructed with missing ratios ranging from 10% to 90%, which also facilitate the future research.

title: FLAME: Flow Guidance and Adaptive Frequency Fusion for All-in-One Mamba-Enhanced Video Restoration
abstract: All-in-One video restoration under adverse weather conditions (e.g., rain, snow, haze) remains challenging, as existing methods either rely on explicit optical flow alignment that becomes unreliable under heavy degradations, or employ implicit sequence modeling that lacks fine-grained temporal correspondence. We propose FLAME, a unified FLow guidance and Adaptive frequency fusion for all-in-one Mamba-Enhanced video restoration framework that synergistically combines explicit alignment with implicit modeling through three core components: (i) Dual-Path Mamba Modeling with complementary Space-Time Sequence Mamba and Hilbert-Sequence Mamba blocks for efficient spatiotemporal modeling with linear-complexity Mamba scanning; (ii) Flow-guided Lightweight Attention featuring degradation-aware flow estimation with triple quality assessment and temporal-spatial attention deformable fusion; (iii) Adaptive Frequency Residual Fusion employing learnable frequency decomposition and cross-channel attention for degradation-specific spectral enhancement. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: 35.50 dB PSNR on VRDS (+3.46 dB over RainMamba), 40.17 dB on LWDDS (+2.96 dB over RainMamba), 31.04 dB on W3 multiweather benchmark (+0.59 dB over AIM-VR), and 29.00 dB on RainSynAll100 rain-haze mixture (+1.33 dB over BasicVSR++), validating the effectiveness of explicit-implicit synergy for diverse weather degradation restoration.

title: BRepDSN: A Dual-stream Network Design for B-Rep Representation Learning Leveraging the Duality of Face and Boundary Vertices
abstract: Designing a neural network for Boundary Representation (B-Rep) models impacts fundamental tasks in Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Engineering (CAE), and Manufacturing (CAM). Existing methods primarily leverage face adjacency for B-Rep feature encoding, overlooking crucial boundary features from the B-Rep vertices. To address this, we introduce a novel dual-stream neural network, called BRepDSN, that explicitly leverages complementary features from both a Face-adjacency Graph (FG) and a Vertex-adjacency Graph (VG). Our method employs alternating message passing between these two graph streams with bidirectional information exchange. Specifically, faces gather boundary-aware cues from incident vertices through a dual mapping, while vertices are refined by face-level context, ensuring boundary-aware and semantically aligned feature encoding. To further boost the performance, we propose a face-vertex contrastive objective. This objective constructs contrastive pairs based on the duality between a face’s embedding and the aggregated embedding of its boundary vertices. Additionally, for segmentation tasks, we use an auxiliary classification loss to determine boundary edges, which acts as a dual task to the main face segmentation. BRepDSN can be used for multiple B-Rep processing tasks. We evaluate the following example tasks: 1) B-Rep Modeling Operation Segmentation, 2) Operation Step Segmentation, 3) B-Rep Classification, 4) Machining Feature Segmentation, and 5) Assembly Mating. Extensive experiments show that our method sets a new state of the art on all five tasks. For example, our method outperforms competing methods on the B-Rep modeling operation segmentation of CC3D (+14.65% mIoU), B-Rep classification of TMCAD (+4.9% oAcc), and the mating task of AutoMate [18] (+23.6% location acc, +21.0% type acc). The code for this paper are available on: https://github.com/shinodashx/BrepDSN.
