title: Individual tree segmentation from terrestrial LiDAR: Benchmarking and forest structural analysis
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Individual tree segmentation from terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) is fundamental to automated forest inventory, yet recent benchmarks have reached divergent conclusions about method performance. We evaluated six methods on TreeScanPL10K, a dataset of 10,417 manually segmented trees across 272 plots of diverse Central European forest. Two are algorithmic (treeX, RayExtract) and four are deep learning (TreeLearn, TreeAIBox, SegmentAnyTree, ForestFormer3D). Beyond aggregate accuracy, we characterized the per-method failure modes and the forest structural attributes that drive performance variation. A clear hierarchy emerged: ForestFormer3D achieved the highest mean IoU (0.76), followed by the other deep-learning methods (0.67–0.71) and the algorithmic approaches (0.60–0.62). Coniferous species were segmented more accurately than broadleaves (0.70 vs. 0.64), with the widest gap for the deep-learning methods. Higher accuracy came at substantial computational cost: 15 min/plot for ForestFormer3D versus under a minute for the fastest methods. To identify what makes a plot difficult to segment, we ran two complementary analyses: one on field-inventory attributes, the other on crown-geometry descriptors derived from the reference annotations. The dominant signal came from crown geometry: the plot-level Mean Crown Area Index (Mean CAI), which summarizes how many crown layers stack vertically above each ground cell, was the strongest single correlate and the top-ranked feature for every method individually. Multi-layered canopies are the hardest to segment. The field-inventory pool added a related but distinct dimension: structural diversity in species composition and spatial arrangement contributed beyond the vertical-layering signal. All six methods degraded in parallel along these gradients, indicating that the evaluated methods share common difficulties in structurally complex stands. We release the exact 2 cm benchmark point clouds, plot-level attributes and results, point-level predictions from all six methods for 18 selected plots, and the evaluation code.

title: How should rural residential land in metropolitan suburbs be governed in the future? Evidence from Beijing using RGB-encoded multidimensional drivers and CNN prediction
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Rural residential land in metropolitan suburbs often expands, stabilizes and contracts within the same region, making static zoning inadequate for anticipatory governance. Existing land-use prediction approaches commonly use attribute vectors or remotely sensed image features, limiting their ability to reduce input dimensionality while preserving the spatial structure and combined effects of locational, accessibility and planning-related drivers. This study converts abstract geospatial drivers into red–green–blue (RGB) images and integrates them with convolutional neural network (CNN) models and ensemble prediction. Using suburban Beijing as a case, we evaluated 78 three-driver configurations across five deep-learning architectures, yielding 390 models. The modified VGG16 model achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.749. The optimal configuration combined village size, distance to the city center and expressway accessibility, indicating that rural residential land change is mainly associated with local development inertia, metropolitan gradients and external connectivity. A model using all nine drivers as nine-band input achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.758, compared with 0.749 for the three-driver RGB model; the latter used substantially fewer drivers while retaining higher precision and clearer variable semantics. Under the 2035 planning scenario, 36.57% of valid grids were predicted to increase, 33.90% to remain unchanged, 0.26% to decrease, and 29.27% were identified as uncertainty areas. These areas require flexible planning, dynamic monitoring and the avoidance of premature rigid decisions. By linking Earth Observation-derived land-change data with spatially structured driver representations, the workflow supports the explanation and prediction of land-use transitions and more adaptive governance of metropolitan suburbs.

title: A spatially and temporally comparable Remote Sensing Ecological Index via de-gradient national PCA for China’s resource-based cities
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Tracking the ecological quality of many cities over many years needs a Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) that stays comparable across space and time, yet standard constructions do not deliver one. A single national principal component analysis (PCA) is dominated by the between-city climate gradient, which loads heat and wetness with the wrong sign and inverts the index. We build a de-gradient national PCA (de-gradient PCA) whose weights come from the within-city component covariance under a fixed global normalization. The resulting index recovers the expected component signs where the single national PCA inverts them. It agrees with MODIS net primary productivity, an external ecological reference (city-mean r = 0.59 ), even after controlling for greenness (partial r = 0.50 ), and its weights are stable to city resampling and to leaving out any representative year. Applied to all 125 prefecture-level resource-based cities of China over 2003–2023, mean RSEI rose from 0.61 to 0.65 ( p < 1 0 − 4 ), with 83% of cities on a rising trend, faster than in 245 non-resource cities. Resource type set the ecological level more than development stage, and 13 cities in the arid northwest and coal belt stayed near 0.30. A spatial Durbin model identifies built-up land as the strongest local pressure and industrial structure as a persistent negative regional spillover; random-forest importance corroborates the built-up ranking.

title: SGDiff-OS: a semantic-guided diffusion model for SAR oil spill scattering and mask field generation
abstract: Marine oil spill remote sensing relies heavily on high-quality annotated data, yet the limited availability of well-annotated SAR oil spill samples with backscatter information and structural labels remains a challenge. To address the lack of structural consistency and scattering representation of existing generation methods, this study proposes a Semantic-Guided Diffusion for SAR Oil Spill Generation model (SGDiff-OS) for the joint generation of SAR oil spill backscatter coefficient σ° and corresponding binary oil spill labels, trained on a self-constructed SAR oil spill dataset. The model adopts a dual-channel conditional diffusion framework and incorporates semantic modulation to encode prior knowledge of spotted, blocky and slender morphologies, thereby improving structural representation and category controllability. Experimental results demonstrate that the generated samples show general agreement with real data in visual quality and overall statistical trends, although measurable distributional differences remain. The global mean σ° differs by approximately 1.96 dB between the real and generated samples. The generated samples retain the lower-backscatter relationship of oil-covered regions relative to seawater, although the oil-water contrast decreases from 6.59 dB to 4.65 dB. Furthermore, in an expert annotation evaluation of generated image mask pairs, the generated masks achieve an mIoU of 0.7658 and an F1-score of 0.8637 when evaluated against reference annotations. Under limited training data conditions, incorporating generated samples leads to a maximum improvement of 24.2% in mIoU, suggesting its potential value for sample augmentation under limited training conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed model can generate SAR oil spill samples with the dominant scattering trends of real SAR data, providing supplementary data for oil spill detection and segmentation tasks.

title: A rapid and robust scheme for CFOSAT SWIM nadir SWH retrieval
abstract: The Surface Waves Investigation and Monitoring (SWIM) onboard the China-France Oceanography Satellite (CFOSAT) has acquired unprecedented global ocean wave direction spectrum information. Additionally, it incorporates a nadir observation mode for significant wave height (SWH) based on principles analogous to conventional altimeters, which serves to calibrate the total energy of the wave spectrum. The retrieval of SWH from such nadir radar observations generally employs theoretical models to retrack the waveforms reflected by the sea surface, a method that demonstrates high accuracy in the open ocean environment. However, obtaining SWH using traditional retracking algorithms is computationally expensive. Furthermore, in coastal regions, waveforms are affected by factors such as the presence of land and sea ice, which means that the SWH retrieval relying on theoretical models often either fails or yields substantial errors. Leveraging the fact that SWIM does not necessitate precise ranging, we bypassed the decades-old retracking paradigm by developing dual neural network inversion models. These models perform direct SWH estimation following an initial classification of SWIM nadir waveforms. The first model targets standard open-sea waveforms, while the second is designed for coastal and sea-ice 'ocean-like' waveforms that deviate from normal patterns yet retain essential wave information. The results show that the normal-ocean model achieves a processing speed over 13 times faster than the MLE4 algorithm and nearly 22 times faster than the adaptive retracking algorithm, while maintaining comparable accuracy (RMSE = 0.31 m) to the SWIM nadir SWH product. Meanwhile, the ocean-like model enhances both the quantity and quality of usable SWH data in non-open ocean areas, leveraging the accurate mapping relationships established by the neural networks. Generally, a rapid and robust scheme was developed in this paper for retrieving nadir SWH from CFOSAT SWIM, providing an alternative methodology for retrieving nadir geophysical parameters in future nadir-looking radar systems.

title: A Neuro-symbolic Framework under Statistical Relational Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Neuro-symbolic systems aim to combine neural learning with symbolic reasoning for building interpretable and generalizable intelligent systems. While recent studies have explored different strategies for neuro-symbolic integration, existing approaches remain limited by (i) the absence of unified learning mechanisms between continuous neural representations and discrete symbolic concepts, (ii) weak interaction between neural prediction and symbolic reasoning, and (iii) restricted reuse of learned concepts for unseen reasoning scenarios. To address these issues, we propose NSF-SRL, a general neuro-symbolic framework based on statistical relational learning. NSF-SRL jointly models neural predictions, latent predicates and first-order logic rules within a unified probabilistic framework. For concept learning, NSF-SRL introduces a neuralized variational inference mechanism that learns predicate-level representations from neural representations and enables efficient neuro-symbolic interaction through variational expectation-maximization optimization. For concept manipulation, NSF-SRL allows learned concepts to be reused and composed with logic rules for interpretable explanation and compositional reasoning. Extensive experiments on digit image addition, zero-shot image classification and visual relationship detection, together with comprehensive analyses, demonstrate the effectiveness, generalization and scalability of NSF-SRL.

title: LLM-Enhanced 3D Generation: A Survey
TAETrack++: Trajectory Age Extension and Motion Refinement for Robust Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) is a vital task in computer vision, involving the continuous tracking and stable identification (ID) of multiple objects across video sequences. Existing methods often focus heavily on identity matching during association, neglecting the quality of trajectories, which affects object tracking performance. This article proposes a trajectory-age optimization approach for MOT that effectively improves its performance. First, we proposed TAE and TG to adaptively extend trajectory lifespans through IoU constraints and position awareness, allowing long-lost objects to be re-associated with their original trajectories instead of being initialized as new tracks, while suppressing erroneous matches. Second, by incorporating the track loss duration, our method enhances the observation-centric re-update mechanism and an adaptive Kalman filter with a dynamic noise scale, thereby reducing ID switches. Finally, our method combines Gaussian process-based interpolation with wavelet-thresholding denoising, leveraging the optimization of global smoothing and local denoising to improve trajectory smoothness and authenticity. Extensive experiments on the MOT17, MOT20, and DanceTrack standard datasets demonstrate that our method is competitive with the current state-of-the-art trackers and offers more robust ID maintenance across various challenging tracking scenarios.

title: Task Interference Mitigation via Confidence-Stratified Classifier Calibration for Prompt-based Continual Learning
abstract: Prompt-based continual learning is a promising direction that effectively leverages the capabilities of pre-trained models. These methods typically learn task-specific prompts and predict task identity to select the prompt during inference. However, task interference caused by prompt misselection significantly constrains their performance. Although several studies have attempted to mitigate this issue, they treat all samples equally, without specifically addressing the samples that are primarily affected by prompt misselection. In this paper, we stratify samples into three distinct categories according to their different responses to prompt misselection, including susceptible samples, refractory samples, and resilient samples. This stratification reveals that misselection-induced interference primarily manifests in susceptible samples, as only their classification correctness is influenced by prompt misselection, while other samples remain unaffected. This realization drives us to design a novel prompt-based approach called Confidence-Stratified Classifier Calibration (CoSC), which harnesses the complementary roles of all categories to safeguard susceptible samples. Specifically, we apply targeted optimization based on the unique properties of each category to cooperatively calibrate classifiers of both the prompt instruction part and the prompt selector, thereby protecting susceptible samples from dual perspectives. Extensive experiments show that CoSC achieves state-of-the-art performance across various benchmarks in class-incremental learning.

title: Fast and Compressed ADA-UNet: Refractive-Index Reconstruction with Latent-Domain Low-Rank Compression
abstract: Optical diffraction tomography (ODT) provides label-free three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) maps, but conventional reconstructions are highly sensitive to speckle noise and severely under-sampled illumination angles. We propose ADA-UNet, a compact two-stage framework in which (i) a modality-specific autoencoder learns a compact representation of stitched diffraction inputs, and (ii) a latent-domain ResUNet maps these interferometric latent codes to RI latent codes for non-iterative reconstruction. For compactness, the interferometry-to-RI mapping is expressed in Dirac form, but the network itself is implemented entirely with standard convolutional operators on GPU hardware. To reduce computational cost without changing the reconstruction objective, low-rank factorization is applied specifically to the ADA-aligned latent mapper. The resulting compressed model, ADA-UNetc, reduces the parameter count from 12.5M to 6.0M (a 52% reduction) while maintaining nearly unchanged reconstruction quality, with SSIM changing from 0.943 to 0.940 and NRMSE from 0.051 to 0.052. Across all evaluated ODT, cross-modal image-synthesis, and adaptation baselines, the proposed model achieves the best overall fidelity and a measured per-volume inference time of 187 s, compared with 221-840 s for the baselines. Experiments on synthetic and real 2-D/3-D data further demonstrate robustness under evaluation-time noise perturbations and sparse-angle acquisition, highlighting the potential of ADA-UNet for efficient and reliable quantitative phase imaging.

Toward a global snow water equivalent observing strategy
abstract: Current snow observations do not meet the data requirements established by the 2017 Decadal Survey and the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS) for global snow water equivalent (SWE) measurements. This paper evaluates existing spaceborne assets for global SWE and snow depth monitoring and identifies critical observational gaps that necessitate a dedicated snow observing strategy. We review snow data requirements across multiple application areas, including water resources, climate monitoring, weather forecasting, and disaster management, demonstrating the need for SWE measurements at 100 m to 4 km spatial resolution with 1- to 5-day temporal frequency and 10–20% accuracy. Analysis of current capabilities from missions including AMSR2, Sentinel-1, NISAR, and ICESat-2 reveals that while these sensors provide valuable SWE and depth information, they cannot, even when combined, deliver the comprehensive, high-resolution SWE data required for operational and scientific applications, observing only 40–60% of the global snowpack on a daily to weekly basis. We propose a global snow observing strategy centered on a core radar-based snow mission that would serve as the reference standard for a constellation of complementary sensors. This approach, combined with existing observations, ancillary data, advanced data fusion techniques, and land surface models, would provide accurate and timely SWE data essential for water resource management, climate research, and hazard mitigation.

title: Hierarchical active learning for annotation-efficient 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing remains challenging because sparse returns, irregular layouts, heavy occlusion, and diverse machinery make object representation and localization difficult. Dense manual annotation in such scenes is also inefficient and costly, creating a strong need for annotation-efficient learning. Existing active-learning methods often struggle in this setting because they tend to favor uncertain but redundant samples while overlooking representative scene coverage. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Clustering-enhanced Active Learning (HCAL), an active-learning framework for LiDAR-based 3D object detection in construction and roadwork environments. HCAL improves sample selection under limited labeling budgets by identifying informative candidate keyframes, suppressing redundant uncertain samples, and preserving representative coverage through entropy filtering, gradient-space clustering, and density-consistency selection. To support field-relevant evaluation, we further establish ConVeh3D as a construction-scene LiDAR benchmark for annotation-efficient 3D detection and unknown-category-aware evaluation in a controlled category-withheld setting. Experiments on ConVeh3D, with KITTI as secondary supporting evidence, show that HCAL achieves the best average detection accuracy across most tested labeling budgets. The results indicate that HCAL provides an effective framework for improving sample efficiency in construction-scene LiDAR-based 3D object detection under limited labeling budgets. The dataset and code will be made available at https://github.com/zxk688/ConVeh3D .

title: PSGRNet: Multi-scale spectral–frequency representation learning with gated residual fusion for coastal wetland classification using UAV hyperspectral imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Coastal wetlands are characterized by diverse vegetation, high spectral similarity, fragmented spatial distributions, and dynamic environmental conditions, posing significant challenges for accurate hyperspectral image classification. Although UAV hyperspectral imagery provides fine-grained spatial and spectral observations that can help capture such complex and fragmented features, effectively leveraging this information to distinguish spectrally similar and spatially intermixed vegetation types remains an open problem. Therefore, we propose a Progressive Spectral Gated Residual Network (PSGRNet). Specifically, a spectral enhancement and multi-scale sequence modeling strategy is first introduced to strengthen discriminative spectral representations and capture multi-scale spectral dependencies. Building on these enhanced representations, a frequency-aware module further exploits global frequency-domain characteristics to aggregate informative spectral features adaptively. To effectively integrate both spectral and frequency-domain representations, a GRF strategy is developed to improve the robustness of the network in heterogeneous and fragmented coastal wetland scenes. We have collected three UAV-based hyperspectral datasets covering representative coastal wetland scenarios, including reed-dominated natural wetlands (NT-YK), highly fragmented landscapes with dynamic land-cover transitions (YC-YS), and human-influenced estuarine environments (LYG-LH). Experimental results on these three datasets demonstrate that PSGRNet outperforms 9 representative methods, achieving macro F1 scores of 89.25%, 81.99%, and 81.29%, respectively. These results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for accurate coastal wetland classification and demonstrate the value of the released datasets. The datasets will be publicly available at https://github.com/HAPPYFST/Wetland-HSI-Data .

title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconstruction as a discriminative ranking problem within the generative output manifold. Our approach maintains perceptual reconstruction as a supervisory signal and integrates a ranking-based discriminative constraint by systematically ordering matched and mismatched reconstruction outputs. This formulation embeds discriminative information seamlessly into the generative process, alleviating the risk of loss competition. Specifically, we propose AUC Generative Reconstruction (AUCGR), which optimizes the area under the ROC curve (AUC) by ensuring higher scores for matched pairs than for mismatched pairs, and Partial AUC Generative Reconstruction (pAUCGR), which addresses supervision bias by focusing on mismatched comparisons within reliable feature subspaces. The proposed objectives are designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural modifications to existing generative reconstruction frameworks. Theoretical analysis establishes rigorous connections to AUC/pAUC optimization and provides generalization guarantees. Extensive experiments across diverse CLIP architectures, more than 30 visual benchmarks, generative backbones, and MLLMs consistently validate that our method advances both discriminative accuracy and fine-grained perceptual representation, establishing a new benchmark for visual representation learning.

title: Stress-Driven Anisotropic Voronoi Structures
abstract: This paper presents a method for constructing anisotropic 3D Voronoi infill structures whose morphology adapts to principal stress directions induced by external loads. Existing stress-aligned infill methods predominantly generate truss-like architectures, whereas wall-like structures are known to achieve higher stiffness at comparable material volume. Our method bridges this gap by enabling the construction of stress-aligned wall-like infills. This is achieved through stress-driven sampling and a Lloyd relaxation constrained by the underlying stress field. A novel adaptive metric, the L q norm, is introduced to compute anisotropic Centroidal Voronoi Tessellations (CVTs) with cells aligned to locally varying stress directions. The final structure is generated by carving shape-preserving harmonic distance fields within the Voronoi cells, producing a continuous wall-like microstructure. The resulting infills outperform existing wall- and truss-based approaches in stiffness at comparable material volume while maintaining substantially lower construction times. We demonstrate these properties through finite-element analyses and physical experiments on 3D printed specimens.

Tracking US tidal marsh extent and change with dense Landsat time series and comparisons with existing products
abstract: Tidal marsh changes encompass both categorical cover change (i.e., extent change) and condition change, such as alterations in vegetation composition and hydrological regime, which together regulate ecosystem resilience and carbon cycling. Yet, most existing products rely on selective image compositing under similar tidal conditions or statistical values over fixed intervals, followed by epoch-based comparisons. These approaches are mainly designed to capture differences in marsh extent, while condition change within the same tidal marsh cover type remains largely unresolved despite its ecological importance. Here, we present a tide-informed dense time-series framework, DEtection and Characterization of cOastal tiDal wEtlands change (DECODE v2), for continuous monitoring of tidal marsh extent and change (including condition change and cover change, such as tidal marsh gain or loss) across the conterminous United States from 1988 to 2023. Two key methodological advances underpin this framework and enable global transferability: integration of a global empirical ocean tide model to estimate water levels for each Landsat observation, and an adaptive temporal normalization strategy to ensure consistent observation density across single- and dual-satellite eras. Stratified random sampling confirms strong performance in both tidal marsh extent and change mapping, supporting a shift from traditional binary extent mapping and extent-only change detection to a continuous monitoring strategy. Cross-product comparisons show that DECODE improves spatial consistency and reduces disagreement with reference interpretation for tidal marsh extent and cover change, while also providing additional information that is largely absent from existing products, including separation of cover change and condition change, change timing, and repeated change events at the same location. Critically, condition change dominated cumulative tidal marsh change across the conterminous United States (CONUS), accounting for approximately 81.1 ± 2.0% of the cumulative annual change area and greatly exceeding cumulative cover change (13,058 ± 1366 km 2 versus 3038 ± 216 km 2 ). By characterizing not only where tidal marsh extent changes occur, but also what type of change occurs, when it occurs, and how often it recurs, DECODE provides a more comprehensive basis for assessing ecosystem resilience, restoration effectiveness, and blue carbon dynamics.

title: DBEFNet: a dual-branch fusion network integrating remote sensing imagery and building morphology for urban village segmentation
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Urban villages (UVs) are informal settlements embedded within Chinese cities, and their boundary delineation is fundamental to urban renewal and refined spatial management. However, accurate segmentation of UVs relies on both visual characteristics and the spatial organization of buildings, yet previous studies have often relied on simplified representations of building morphology that inadequately capture spatial configuration. We propose DBEFNet, a dual-branch encoding and fusion framework that exploits remote sensing imagery (RSI) and building morphology heatmaps for fine-grained UVs segmentation. The RSI branch combines CNN and Swin Transformer encoders with multi-scale feature extraction to capture and integrate local appearance and broader spatial context. In the Building branch, multiple building attributes are transformed into morphology heatmaps and adaptively weighted to characterize building-cluster patterns. A hybrid attention fusion module (HAFM) models bidirectional dependencies between visual semantics and building morphology. Experiments across 15 cities yielded an overall accuracy (OA) of 94.79 % and a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 86.24 %. Ablation experiments indicate that incorporating building morphology improves mIoU by 0.87 % over the enhanced RSI-only model, while adding the HAFM provides further gains of 0.93 %. Compared with the RSI-only model, DBEFNet achieved higher mIoU in 11 of the 15 cities, with an average city-wise gain of 1.92 %. Trained on Beijing, DBEFNet achieved 75.79 % mean mIoU across 12 unseen target cities, demonstrating its cross-city generalization capability. These results underscore the critical role of building morphology and the value of integrating morphological cues with visual appearance for precise UVs mapping.

title: Application of Mobile-DOAS observations for analyzing sub-pixel variability and comparing TROPOMI-derived NO x emissions over the Yeosu-Gwangyang industrial complex
abstract: This study investigates sub-pixel spatial variability in TROPOMI NO2 observations and its impact on the consistency between TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS observations for the Yeosu-Gwangyang industrial complex in South Korea. Furthermore, NOx emissions are estimated using both datasets and compared with a bottom-up emission inventory. The comparison of co-located TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS observations shows good correlation (r = 0.86), with TROPOMI data exhibiting a slight underestimation relative to the Mobile-DOAS observations (-8.5%). The underestimation was more pronounced when Mobile-DOAS observations had limited spatial coverage within the satellite pixel and was reduced when the spatial coverage increased, indicating the importance of spatial representativeness of ground-based measurements. The analysis of TROPOMI NO2 columns with the Exponentially Modified Gaussian (EMG) emission analysis reveals a decreasing trend in NOx emissions from 2021 to 2025 (-29%), along with pronounced seasonal variability. In comparison, Mobile-DOAS-derived emissions show substantial variability across individual measurement rounds and no clear seasonal pattern. A comparison of TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS emission estimates with bottom-up emission inventory data indicates reasonable comparability, although differences vary across the observation periods. The weekend-to-weekday emission ratios range from 0.80 to 0.90, indicating a weak weekend effect consistent with the industrial characteristics of the region. Overall, this study highlights that (1) sub-pixel variability affects the consistency between satellite and ground-based observations and should be explicitly accounted for in satellite validation studies, and (2) satellite, Mobile-DOAS, and bottom-up estimates provide complementary information for quantifying NOx emissions over industrial regions.

title: Coarse-to-fine physics-guided reconstruction of gridded sea level anomalies from HY-2B/C/D altimetry
abstract: The capability of the Chinese HY-2B/C/D altimeter constellation for gridded sea level anomaly (SLA) reconstruction using only HY-2 observations remains insufficiently evaluated. This study presents a physics-guided framework designed for near-real-time (NRT) SLA reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific and retrospectively evaluates it using 2022−2025 HY-2B/C/D observations. The framework combines an OI-derived coarse background with deep-learning refinement, with target-period reconstruction driven solely by HY-2B/C/D along-track data. Validation against an identical set of 1255 independent tide-gauge observations yields mean RMSE of 0.051 m and a mean correlation coefficient (r) of 0.83 over 12 tide-gauge stations. Inter-product comparisons during 2022−2025 show closer agreement with the DUACS DT and NRT products than with NSOAS, although differences in SLA reference conventions and geophysical correction standards among the products should be considered when interpreting regional discrepancies. Scale-dependent evaluation using SARAL/AltiKa along-track observations indicates a mean effective spatial resolution of approximately 300 km. Dynamical consistency is further assessed against surface-drifter observations using geostrophic velocity anomaly magnitude, yielding mean RMSE of 0.181 m s−1 and r of 0.54. These results demonstrate that spatially coherent and dynamically plausible daily SLA fields can be reconstructed with HY-2B/C/D as the sole altimetric observations during the target period, supporting the potential of the proposed framework for NRT SLA reconstruction under sparse observational constraints.

title: Gravity-conditioned diffusion for seafloor bathymetric resolution enhancement
abstract: Global bathymetric products such as SRTM15+ provide extensive ocean coverage but cannot resolve many fine-scale seafloor features captured by shipborne multibeam surveys. Generative reconstruction methods can reconstruct more detailed terrain, but they may also introduce plausible-looking structures that are not supported by observations. We propose GravBathy-Diff, a conditional diffusion framework that uses observed low-resolution bathymetry as its primary input and incorporates satellite-altimetry-derived marine gravity as an auxiliary physical constraint. The gravity-differential enhancement module jointly encodes bathymetry, terrain derivatives, and the co-registered gravity field at the input stage. Gravity-conditioned time–frequency modulation regulates the contribution of gravity across diffusion stages and feature bands, while gravity-guided attention focuses this information on the spatial locations and feature channels where it is most useful. Deflections of the vertical, gravity anomalies, and vertical gravity gradients derived from Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) wide-swath altimetry are compared as alternative conditioning fields. Experiments are conducted on real SRTM15+ –multibeam bathymetry pairs from four ocean regions and assessed using depth error, perceptual similarity, terrain derivatives, and spectral fidelity. GravBathy-Diff achieves the strongest overall performance among the evaluated regression, adversarial, and diffusion methods, with the exception of one regional gradient-RMSE result. It ranks first on all six metrics averaged over four additional ocean areas and remains effective on an independent public digital elevation model (DEM) benchmark at 4×. Among the three gravity representations, the vertical gravity gradient provides the most effective guidance for reconstructing local relief. These results show that marine gravity can support the recovery of fine-scale seafloor structure while reducing high-frequency artifacts that are inconsistent with the available observations.

title: Correction

End-to-End Differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics for Fluid--Rigid Optimization with Gradient Stabilization
abstract: We introduce an end-to-end differentiable optimization framework for Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with fluid–rigid body coupling. The central difficulty is not only to obtain local derivatives of SPH operators, but also to propagate useful sensitivities through long rollouts whose particle neighborhoods, contacts, and pressure responses change rapidly over time. These effects make reverse-mode gradients noisy and often cause adjoint variables to explode in long-horizon control and inverse-design tasks. We formulate an SPH-specific reverse-mode pipeline for IISPH-based fluid–rigid simulation and implement the required vector–Jacobian products within checkpointed simulation segments. To make the resulting gradients usable for optimization, we introduce a self-adaptive adjoint correction sequence that acts as a descent-preserving preconditioner: it bounds pathological adjoint amplification while keeping the update direction aligned with the original reverse-mode sensitivity. Our experiments cover a sequence of increasingly demanding tasks, from low-dimensional impulse and shape optimization to scalar-amplitude water actuation, multi-object water-jet balancing, and neural fluid-mediated pendulum control. These results demonstrate that stabilized reverse-mode differentiation can support challenging SPH-based optimization problems involving indirect momentum transfer, long-horizon event timing, and high-dimensional control.

title: Geometrical cross-attention and nonvoid voxelization for efficient 3D medical image segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of 3D medical scans is crucial for clinical diagnostics and treatment planning, yet existing methods often fail to achieve both high accuracy and computational efficiency across diverse anatomies and imaging modalities. To address these challenges, we propose GCNV-Net, a novel 3D medical segmentation framework that integrates a Tri-directional Dynamic Nonvoid Voxel Transformer (3DNVT), a Geometrical Cross-Attention module (GCA), and Nonvoid Voxelization (NV). The 3DNVT block groups nonvoid voxels through axis-wise coordinate sorting along the three spatial axes, enabling effective modeling of complex 3D spatial dependencies. The GCA module incorporates encoded voxel coordinates into multi-scale feature fusion. Meanwhile, the Nonvoid Voxelization reduces computation by discarding embedded locations with negligible feature responses. Relative to the dense-embedding variant, it reduces FLOPs by 56.13% and latency by approximately 68.5% under the controlled 12 8 3 profiling configuration. We evaluate GCNV-Net on multiple widely used benchmarks: BraTS2021, ACDC, MSD Prostate, MSD Pancreas, and AMOS2022. In the primary benchmark comparison, GCNV-Net achieves the highest mean Dice among the compared baseline methods on each of the five datasets. The observed improvements on individual benchmarks reach up to 0.65 percentage points in Dice, 0.63 percentage points in IoU, 1 percentage point in NSD, and a 14.5% relative reduction in HD95. These results support a competitive accuracy-efficiency trade-off on the evaluated public benchmarks.

title: Hyperspectral remote sensing of cover crop traits for decision support in precision nitrogen management
abstract: Spaceborne hyperspectral sensors offer opportunities to quantify crop traits and inform variable rate nitrogen management, yet their operational use remains limited. We evaluated PRISMA and EMIT imagery across four winter cover crop seasons in Maryland, U.S., to predict traits required by the open source Cover Crop Nitrogen Calculator (CC-NCALC) decision support tool. Traits included aboveground biomass, nitrogen concentration (N%), non-structural carbohydrates (NSC%), holocellulose (HCL%), and lignin (LIG%). Using these traits as inputs, the CC-NCALC estimates nitrogen credits from cover crops based on decomposition dynamics informed by trait data, soil, and weather conditions. Nitrogen credits are the estimated amount of plant available nitrogen that a cover crop contributes to the subsequently planted cash crop. Trait models were developed using partial least squares regression with several cross validation strategies. Biomass ( R 2 = 0.70–0.87; RMSE = 661–951 kg ha −1 ), NSC% ( R 2 = 0.69–0.72; RMSE = 4.53–7.63%), and HCL% ( R 2 = 0.65–0.70; RMSE = 5.04–7.50%) predictions were strong. But HCL% and NSC% predictions degraded under cross-scene and cross-species validation ( R 2 = 0.47–0.54; RMSE = 6.06–9.18%). N% ( R 2 = 0.15–0.79; RMSE = 0.46–0.74%) and LIG% ( R 2 = 0.02–0.35; RMSE = 1.22–1.83%) predictions were more variable; predictions using EMIT were more accurate than predictions using PRISMA, but both approaches demonstrated the need for further increases in accuracies of retrieval approaches for these two traits. Spring trait maps from April 2024 were ingested into the CC-NCALC to estimate nitrogen credits, which ranged from −14.58 to 45.65 kg N ha −1 , with higher values associated with greater legume biomass. Inter-scene comparisons demonstrate EMIT's increased spectral fidelity and trait prediction accuracy compared to PRISMA. Results demonstrate that integrating spaceborne hyperspectral imagery with decision support systems can generate site-specific nitrogen credit maps, advancing hyperspectral remote sensing toward operational nutrient management. Future missions will be critical to help scale these approaches for routine on-farm use.

title: Spatiotemporal variability in seasonal and interannual InSAR-derived excess ground ice content retrievals using Sentinel-1
abstract: The melting of excess ground ice in ice-rich permafrost regions causes elevated ground subsidence through soil thaw consolidation at landscape scales. The increased subsidence due to melting of excess ice is unaccounted for in current InSAR-based retrievals of season thaw depth, or active layer thickness (ALT); this omission may lead to overapproximated ALT estimates compared to in situ. We processed Sentinel-1 interferometric data spanning 2018–2023 over the Drew Point and Teshekpuk Lake region. Using a novel degree-day of thaw regression on InSAR displacement time series, we estimated total seasonal subsidence and found elevated subsidence during warmer years which we attribute to the melting of excess ice. Integrating these seasonal subsidence estimates into the remotely sensed active layer thickness (ReSALT) algorithm yielded consistently overapproximated ALT estimates. In conjunction with independent estimates of ALT, we exploited this positive bias in ReSALT to estimate excess ice within the active layer. We found agreement between InSAR estimates of excess ice and in situ measurements within uncertainty for warmer years. We observed a positive spatial correlation between seasonal subsidence and excess ice in the active layer with proximity to surface hydrological features. Furthermore, we observed that InSAR-derived subsidence decreases with older drained lakes, and InSAR-derived excess ice decreases with increasingly degraded ice wedge polygon type. We discovered that thaw season intensity has a first order effect on the temporal variability of seasonal subsidence and excess ice content, and the success of our method is contingent upon warm thaw seasons.

title: High resolution sediment-specific surface soil moisture retrieval using Sentinel-1 time series and auxiliary data
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: In this study, we examine the potential of continuous ground moisture monitoring over a mining site using a combination of in-situ soil moisture sensors and multi-sensor SAR images. We focus on assessing and improving methodologies for retrieval of surface soil moisture, i.e. ground moisture, from SAR measurements focusing on detailed in situ reference observations for several key geomaterials, i.e. sediments, typical in the study site. The mining site represents a limestone quarry located in the southeastern Finland. Our hypothesis is that sediment-specific well-calibrated models can be instrumental in improving soil moisture retrieval under different weather conditions to produce spatially explicit soil moisture estimates at high resolution compared to baseline approaches. Studied SAR data are represented by Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band images, while auxiliary datasets include optical Sentinel-2 data. Reference data were collected using IoT enabled capacitance sensors. The reference data were calibrated based on laboratory analyses conducted on the different sediment types studied, including organic soil, clay, gravel, and flotation sand. The examined machine learning (ML) methods include XGBoost, LightGBM, random forest, support vector regression, linear regression and k-nearest neighbors. The performance of ML algorithms was evaluated using different cross-validation techniques including a five-fold approach as well as Leave-One-Sensor-Out (LOSO) to assess predictive accuracy and transferability to unseen sensors. The best performance under random five-fold cross-validation was achieved with the most comprehensive feature set which combines Sentinel-1 backscatter, time-series based soil moisture indices (SMI), Sentinel-2 optical, topographic, and temperature predictors. SHAP analysis revealed that SAR based features such as VH backscatter, traditional SMI derived from VV backscatter, and incidence angle were among the most important multi-source predictors. Adding sediment information improved Sentinel-1-only retrievals by more than 2 vol-%, but provided little additional benefit when richer multi-source feature sets were used. In the best sediment-area-level configurations, RMSE decreased to 0.037–0.050 m 3 m − 3 (3.7-5.0 vol. % points ), with R 2 values reaching 0.90. Accuracy varied by sediment texture, with the lowest errors for clay and organic soil and higher errors for flotation sand and gravel. However, LOSO validation demonstrated substantially weaker and site-dependent transferability: R 2 ranged from 0.45 to 0.67 for organic soil at a southern site and from 0.07 to 0.21 for organic soil at a northern site. Thus, high within-dataset predictive accuracy did not translate uniformly to unseen sensor locations, highlighting the need for broader spatially independent validation.

title: Process-informed deep learning for interpretable forested wetland mapping under dense canopy
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Canopy-obscured hydrologic signals and gradual wetland–upland transitions hinder the delineation of forested wetlands, particularly when heterogeneous Earth-observation evidence is fused as an unstructured feature stack. We developed a process-informed multi-stream convolutional neural network (CNN) for mapping forested wetlands on a 10-m modelling grid in the Changbai Mountains, China. The model used 85 covariates derived from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, and Copernicus DEM GLO-30. These covariates were assigned a priori to five predictor streams and processed by separate CNN branches before fusion. Relative to a capacity-matched single-stream baseline, the grouped architecture increased forested-wetland F1 by 3.42 percentage points across five validation folds, whereas the gain on the fixed held-out test set was smaller (+1.03 percentage points). For map production, the probability-averaged five-fold ensemble achieved an overall accuracy of 0.873, a macro-F1 of 0.882, and a forested-wetland F1 of 0.836 on the fixed held-out test set. To interpret correlated predictors, group-aggregated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and k-nearest-neighbor conditional replacement were used to characterize global and conditional model reliance. Among correctly classified forested-wetland samples, global reliance was greatest for temporal features and phenology, whereas conditional replacement indicated the greatest residual model reliance for hydrology, followed by topography. Direct pixel counting yielded a map-derived forested-wetland area of 686.6 km 2 , concentrated mainly in peripheral plains and hills. This framework combines process-informed feature organization with dependence-aware interpretation to support interpretable regional mapping of canopy-obscured forested wetlands.

title: Generative Point Cloud Registration With Match-ControlNet
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel 3D registration paradigm, Generative Point Cloud Registration, which bridges advanced 2D generative models with 3D matching tasks to enhance registration performance. Our key idea is to generate cross-view consistent image pairs that are well-aligned with the source and target point clouds, enabling geometry-color feature fusion to facilitate robust matching. To ensure high-quality matching, the generated image pair should feature both 2D-3D geometric consistency and cross-view texture consistency. To this end, we introduce DepthMatch-ControlNet and LiDARMatch-ControlNet, two matching-specific, controllable 2D generative models. Specifically, for depth camera-based 3D registration with point clouds derived from the depth maps, DepthMatch-ControlNet leverages the depth-conditioned generation capabilities of ControlNet to synthesize perspective-view RGB images that are geometrically consistent with depth maps, ensuring accurate 2D-3D alignment. Additionally, by incorporating a coupled conditional denoising scheme and coupled prompt guidance, it further promotes cross-view feature interaction, guiding texture consistency generation. To address LiDAR-based 3D registration with point clouds captured by LiDAR sensors, LiDARMatch-ControlNet extends this framework by conditioning on paired equirectangular range maps projected from 360$^\circ$ LiDAR point clouds, generating corresponding panoramic RGB images. Our generative 3D registration paradigm is general and can be seamlessly integrated into a wide range of existing registration methods to improve their performance. Extensive experiments on the 3DMatch and ScanNet datasets (for depth-camera settings), as well as the Dur360BEV dataset (for LiDAR settings), demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Image Quality Assessment for Machine-oriented Communication
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: The rapid development of Multimoal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has driven the evolution of communication paradigms, making the transmission of visual information in extremely low-bandwidth possible. However, as it is oriented toward computer vision tasks rather than humans, there is no widely accepted metric for its evaluation. To address this issue, we conduct a comprehensive visual quality assessment of machine oriented communication systems. Specifically, we (1) at the source level: a generative codec framework is established, with a MLLM communication pipeline through cross-modal generation between images and text. (2) at the channel level: images are transmitted using channel encoding/decoding strategies in different physical environments, and construct a dataset with 12k pairs of reference/distorted images. (3) at the sink level: 50 computer vision models are implemented to conduct 600k inferences on 5 downstream tasks, to characterize the differences between refer ence/distorted image pairs. (4) at the evaluation level: benchmark 18 cutting-edge Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods, and develop a novel Mixture-of-Experts metric, termed CFA-MoE, to serve as a strong baseline for this task. Experimental results show that the current IQA algorithms cannot accurately evaluate machine-oriented distortions, highlighting the importance and challenge of this task. It is expected this dataset and baseline to facilitate future IQA algorithms and promote the communication paradigms from human to machine preference. Code will be available at: https://github.com/aiben-ch/MoQAD.

title: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
abstract: Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible objects. Unlike traditional 3D objectives that focus on precise metric prediction (e.g., surface normal estimation), SpaRRTa probes a fundamental capability underpinning more advanced forms of human-like spatial understanding. SpaRRTa generates an arbitrary number of photorealistic images with diverse scenes and fully controllable object arrangements, along with freely accessible spatial annotations. Evaluating a range of state-of-the-art VFMs, we reveal significant disparities in their ability to encode directional spatial relations. Through our analysis, we provide insights into the mechanisms that support or hinder this form of spatial awareness in modern VFMs. We hope that SpaRRTa will serve as a useful tool for guiding the development of future spatially aware visual models. Our project page can be found at https://sparrta.gmum.net/.

title: LEAD++: Unsupervised Fine-Grained Visual Representation Learning with Multi-context Enhanced Entropy-Based Adaptive Distillation
Block-Wise Variable Conditional Diffusion for High-Fidelity Text-to-4D Generation
abstract: Text-to-4D scene generation is currently impeded by three primary challenges: the prohibitive memory cost of training high-dimensional diffusion models, the semantic misalignment arising from the failure to disentangle static object identity from dynamic motion in text conditioning, and the scarcity of high-quality datasets that accurately correlate subjects, motions, and environments. To surmount these challenges, we present Swin4D, an end-to-end framework for efficient and high-fidelity text-to-4D synthesis. First, we introduce a Block-wise Variable Conditional Diffusion strategy, which mitigates memory constraints and prevents overfitting by dynamically reconfiguring spatial dependencies during training. Second, we propose Global–Local Alignment, a hierarchical guidance mechanism that explicitly disentangles global scene context from local subject-action semantics via separate T5 and CLIP encoders, ensuring spatiotemporal consistency and fine-grained semantic fidelity regardless of prompt length. Finally, we address data limitations by curating RealSynth4D, a large-scale hybrid dataset combining 108k real-world captures with 72k AI-synthesised scenes, establishing robust correlations between subjects, actions, and complex backgrounds to significantly enhance model generalisation.

A novel approach for soil moisture retrieval via fusing multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations in entire Tibetan Plateau
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Spaceborne GNSS-Reflectometry (GNSS-R) is a powerful technology for soil moisture (SM) retrieval. However, complex topography and steep slopes over the Tibetan Plateau lead to significant signal loss and sampling sparsity. This study proposes a novel Dirichlet-prior-guided Vision Transformer (DG-ViT) framework to fuse multi-source observations from CYGNSS, Tianmu-1, and the FY-3E/F/G constellation. The novel DG-ViT framework incorporates land cover informed prior guidance into multi-spaceborne surface reflectivity (SR) fusion, and its performance is evaluated against single-source retrievals and traditional machine learning algorithms. To assess generalization, the fused SR was coupled with six mainstream machine learning algorithms (RF, XGBoost, ANN, BP, SVM, and GBDT) for 9 km daily SM retrieval, with multi-scale validation conducted against ERA5 SM and nine in-situ stations. Results demonstrate that the DG-ViT framework achieves a daily SR coverage of 89.49 %, representing an improvement of 20.13 % and 14.32 % over standalone CYGNSS and Tianmu-1 data, respectively. In addition, this fusion strategy overcomes the coverage gap of CYGNSS north of 38°N and compensates for the inability of individual FY-3 missions to support daily SM retrieval. In comparative assessments, the DG-ViT combined with RF yields superior performance (R = 0.955, RMSE = 0.039 cm 3 /cm 3 , bias = 0.000 cm 3 /cm 3 ), markedly enhancing retrieval accuracy relative to results derived from single-source CYGNSS or Tianmu-1 SR. In-situ validation shows ubRMSE values between 0.0232 and 0.0619 cm 3 /cm 3 , a 15.1 % precision gain over ERA5 SM. The proposed DG-ViT combined with RF approach effectively exploits the complementarity among multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations over the entire Tibetan Plateau, thereby compensating for the signal deficiencies of individual missions. This fusion approach provides a novel perspective for SM retrieval in high-altitude areas, specifically improving daily SR coverage and SM retrieval accuracy through fusion of multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations with land cover informed prior guidance.

title: ObsGate-SST: observation-gated background–detail learning for global daily sea surface temperature reconstruction
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Infrared cloud screening and incomplete sampling limit the process-scale use of daily satellite sea surface temperature (SST), whereas many gap-filled Level-4 analyses attenuate narrow fronts, tropical-cyclone cold wakes and short-lived warm extremes. This study presents ObsGate-SST, an observation-gated background–detail learning framework for global daily SST reconstruction. The model ingests cloud-contaminated ODYSSEA L3S SST, a valid-pixel mask and an OISST v2.1 prior. A low-frequency branch estimates the basin-scale thermal background, a high-frequency branch reconstructs gradient and texture residuals from observed pixels, and a deterministic observation gate copies all valid satellite observations exactly so that inference is restricted to missing open-ocean pixels. Training used 2000–2020 daily fields, validation used 2021–2022 and independent testing used 2023–2025. Against 2023 quality-level-5 iQuam matchups, monthly bias ranged from 0.193 to 0.291 °C, RMSE from 0.637 to 0.849 °C and correlation from 0.993 to 0.996 across 902,665 collocations. A cloud-gap-shaped withheld-observed-pixel audit isolated inferred-pixel skill: ObsGate-SST achieved the lowest pooled RMSE (0.4802 °C), while removing the low-frequency branch, high-frequency branch, gradient/detail loss and physical/prior regularization increased RMSE by 17.0 %, 9.9 %, 3.9 % and 2.0 %, respectively. Relative to DINEOF, U-Net, Swin-Unet and SegNet under common masks, ObsGate-SST better retained spectral energy, frontal continuity, marine-heatwave structure, typhoon cold wakes and equatorial Pacific gradients. These results support observation-gated multiscale learning as a physically interpretable strategy for reconstructing incomplete satellite SST without sacrificing observed-pixel fidelity.

title: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 responses to Hansen-reported forest loss in the Peruvian Amazon: Timing and spatial sensitivity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Satellite signals preceding recorded tropical forest loss are rarely tested against locations without loss. We compared the timing of Sentinel-1 co-polarised (VV) and cross-polarised (VH) backscatter and three Sentinel-2 indices (Normalized Burn Ratio, NBR; Normalized Difference Moisture Index, NDMI; Normalized Difference Red Edge index, NDRE) with Hansen Global Forest Change loss years in the Ucayali Region of the Peruvian Amazon (2019–2025). Hansen loss years served as an annual, satellite-derived reference rather than independent ground truth. Monthly time series at 819 locations with Hansen loss in 2021–2024 at the central 30 m pixel were compared with 2,588 non-loss locations using before-after analysis, superposed epoch analysis and single-change-point breakpoint detection with a pseudo-year null model. Sensitivity to spatial matching was tested with 50–250 m buffers, and canopy height from the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation was examined exploratorily. All variables declined around the Hansen loss year relative to non-loss locations, most strongly for Sentinel-2 (Cliff’s δ = − 0.66 to − 0.76; Sentinel-1: −0.27 to − 0.30). Negative breakpoints occurred at 74–82% of loss locations for the Sentinel-2 indices, mostly in the loss year. Breakpoints preceding the loss year occurred at 9.5–19.0% of loss locations, exceeding the non-loss comparison only for NBR (+4.9 percentage points) and NDRE (+3.8) at the primary penalty. Apparent pre-loss rates increased with buffer size and depended on breakpoint selection, and exploratory GEDI analysis found no detectable association between canopy height and breakpoint timing. Pre-loss satellite signals should be tested against non-loss baselines before being interpreted as early warning.

title: Integrating vegetation phenology and SWOT-derived surface water dynamics for improved county-scale winter wheat yield prediction
abstract: Winter wheat yield is shaped by crop growth status and surface hydrological conditions. However, remote-sensing approaches based primarily on vegetation index (VI) time series may not fully represent the surrounding surface-water environment in county-scale yield prediction. We integrated growth-stage VI features with surface-water dynamics derived from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission to predict county-level winter wheat yield in Henan Province, China. We evaluated direct feature fusion, same-year residual correction, and target-year residual correction following cross-year VI extrapolation using outer ten-fold cross-validation. Inner five-fold cross-fitting generated same-year VI residual targets exclusively within each outer training set. The VI-only model achieved R2 = 0.772, RMSE = 0.688 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.510 t ha−1. Direct incorporation of SWOT features reduced predictive accuracy, with R2 = 0.749, RMSE = 0.721 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.547 t ha−1. By contrast, SWOT-based residual correction yielded a clearer improvement in same-year prediction, increasing R2 to 0.795 and reducing RMSE to 0.652 t ha−1. The historical VI model was trained on 2010–2021, independently tested on 2022–2023, and extrapolated to 2024, where it achieved R2 = 0.676, RMSE = 0.819 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.611 t ha−1. Calibrated using observed 2024 yields from training counties and evaluated on held-out 2024 counties, subsequent target-year residual correction with concurrent SWOT features increased R2 to 0.749 and reduced RMSE and MAE to 0.722 and 0.524 t ha−1, respectively. SHAP analysis showed that SWOT contributions were concentrated during seeding, emergence, overwintering, green, heading–flowering, and filling and varied by spatial scale and prediction scenario. Overall, SWOT-derived surface-water observations provided complementary predictive information relative to the evaluated VI baselines, particularly for target-year spatial calibration. Their broader applicability across regions, crops, and years remains to be established through independent validation.

title: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range: Fusion of Face, Body Shape and Gait
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: We address the problem of whole-body person recognition in unconstrained environments. This problem arises in surveillance scenarios such as those in the IARPA Biometric Recognition and Identification at Altitude and Range (BRIAR) program, where biometric data is captured at long standoff distances, elevated viewing angles, and under adverse atmospheric conditions (e.g., turbulence and high wind velocity). To this end, we propose FarSight, a unified end-to-end system for person recognition that integrates complementary biometric cues across face, gait, and body shape modalities. FarSight comprises four core modules: multi-subject detection and tracking, recognition-aware video restoration, modality-specific biometric feature encoding, and quality-guided multi-modal fusion. Rather than treating these modules as independent processing stages, FarSight coordinates key stage-level decisions around the final biometric objective: tracking maintains identity-consistent temporal evidence, restoration is selectively invoked and optimized for recognition, and modality-quality estimates guide score fusion. This coordinated design supports recognition under degraded image conditions, large pose and scale variations, and cross-domain gaps. Extensive experiments on the BRIAR dataset, one of the most comprehensive benchmarks for long-range, multi-modal biometric recognition, demonstrate the effectiveness of FarSight. Compared with our preliminary system [1] on the Face-Included treatment set of BRIAR EVP 5.0.1, the current system improves 1:1 verification (TAR@0.1% FAR) by 34.4 percentage points and closed-set identification (Rank-20) by 17.8 percentage points, while reducing open-set identification errors (FNIR@1% FPIR) by 34.3 percentage points. Furthermore, FarSight was evaluated in the 2025 NIST RTE Face in Video Evaluation (FIVE), which conducts standardized face recognition testing on the BRIAR dataset. These results establish FarSight as a state-of-the-art solution for operational biometric recognition in challenging real-world conditions.

title: Representation of Directed Acyclic Graphs by Sequences of Instructions for Symbolic Regression
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Symbolic Regression (SR) aims to discover a closed-form mathematical expression that fits an observed dataset by representing those expressions as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). A DAG with k internal nodes admits Θ(k!) equivalent node orderings of the same expression, so structurally identical candidates repeatedly reach the fitness evaluator of the solver model, consuming search budget. We introduce ISALSR (Instruction Set and Language for Symbolic Regression), an encoding that maps every labeled DAG to a canonical string over a two-tier alphabet of structural and operation-labeled tokens. Canonical strings are reached via a greedy algorithm guided by 1-Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) subtree hashing. We prove that the canonical string is a complete labeled-DAG invariant under a reachability condition: two expressions share their string if and only if their DAGs are isomorphic. ISALSR integrates at the evaluation boundary and needs no change to the host search algorithm. It has been validated on a systematic enumerator (UDFS) and an evolutionary search (Bingo) over a 70-problem suite assembled from nine published benchmarks, against both the host solvers' native representation and a naive hash of a fixed-order DAG serialization. Canonicalization eliminates a mean of 38.1% of evaluations on UDFS and 43.7% on Bingo, on every one of the 70 problems under both hosts. A paired test across problems puts its reduction factor above that of the naive hash at a Cohen's d of 2.54 and 7.05, both at p < 10-12. Canonicalization consumes 0.04% of run time on UDFS and 16.1% on Bingo. Deduplication is therefore close to free where a fitness evaluation costs orders of magnitude more than a canonical string, and expensive where the two are comparable. ISALSR is the first instruction-based graph encoding to carry operation labels, edge direction and a non-commutative operator, and because the canonical form is itself a string, it also gives sequence models a target that is invariant to node renumbering. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/MarioPasc/IsalSR.

title: A Simple but Efficient Method to Achieve High Performance with Extreme Sparsity
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Pruning effectively removes redundant parameters and computations from neural networks, reduces model storage space, and saves time, memory, and energy during the training and inference phases. However, current pruning methods perform well at moderate and high sparsity, but the performance difference with dense network models at extreme sparsity is huge. In order to bridge the accuracy gap between extremely sparse and dense models, this paper proposes a simple but efficient pruning strategy-Tensor Decomposition Based Iterative Magnitude Pruning (TDIMP) method. This strategy uses tensor theory to optimize the model structure before IMP to reduce the search space of the sparse subnetwork during pruning, thus improving the hit rate of the optimal sparse subnetwork. Specifically, firstly, the weight matrix or weight tensor of the dense model is represented as a low-rank tensor decomposition format, and the feature extraction capability of the base module is enhanced by multi-step chaining operations to construct a low-rank compact network model. Secondly, IMP is performed on the low-rank model. The weight updates are sampled multiple times at the later stages of model training during each magnitude pruning process to smooth the oscillations of the learning trajectory and improve the performance of the sparse model. To evaluate the superiority of TDIMP, we first conducted extensive experiments using LSTM, VGGNet, ResNet, and Transformer architectures on UCF11, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet datasets at sparsities ranging from 98% to 99.9%, and compared it with state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show that TDIMP has higher accuracy, faster inference and less storage space than the pruning at initialization, dynamic sparse training, and iterative pruning methods in the extreme sparse case. In addition, TDIMP also has faster training speed than IMP methods.

title: 2D Gaussian Splatting for Semantic Segmentation via Discrete-to-Continuous Representation toward Boundary-Preserving Feature Upsampling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: High-quality semantic segmentation requires not only rich semantic understanding but also precise delineation of object boundaries. While prevailing methods rely on discrete feature representations that often lead to boundary misalignment, jagged contours, and blurry edges along complex contours, we present GSSeg, a novel semantic segmentation paradigm based on Gaussian Splatting that has been successfully applied to 3D scene reconstruction. Specifically, GSSeg reformulates the discrete feature space as continuous Gaussian fields, thereby rendering spatial continuity modeling to produce high-quality segmentation results. However, directly adapting 2DGS to existing pipelines suffers from the structural granularity loss in low-resolution features and the inherent low-pass limitations of Gaussian rendering. To address the insufficient structural granularity available for discrete-to-continuous transformation, we propose the cross-layer neighborhood interaction scheme utilizing alternating global scanning, which establishes cross-scale contextual cues to enhance adaptive Gaussian kernel generation. Additionally, addressing the inherent low-pass limitations of Gaussian rendering, we introduce spatial uncertainty-aware resampling driven by resolution bias estimation, which selectively compensates for high-frequency details attenuated during Gaussian rendering. Furthermore, we introduce an effective Gaussian kernel initialization strategy that approximates Gaussian radial basis function interpolation, ensuring model training stability. Comprehensive experiments on standard benchmarks, especially high-resolution matting-level dataset MaSS13K, demonstrate that GSSeg achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: Seeing Text Clearly in the Dark: Unifying Localization and Enhancement via Deep Morphological Synergy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Low-light text localization, an interdisciplinary field, has gained significant attention recently. The goal is to provide enhanced text locational information beneficial for both machine and human vision. Existing one-stage and two-stage methods either rely on single detectors specially designed for low-light conditions or on a simple cascade of detectors and enhancers, both of which exhibit limitations in effectively addressing the joint task of enhancement and text localization simultaneously. Relying solely on a single set of dual operations in deep morphology, we link the joint task via a bidirectional morphological sync bridge that ensures the simultaneous flow of two directions: one preserving the topological connectivity of text and the other improving its exposure level under low-light conditions. We then introduce a novel bi-level synergistic learning strategy, where text localization serves as the upper-level task and enhancement as the lower-level task. This strategy leverages bidirectional connectivity in the deep morphological sync bridge as a learnable constraint and alternately updates coupled gradients with different update frequencies to optimize the joint task. Extensive experiments on the low-light text localization dataset LATeD demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both tasks. The code will be released.

title: Kernel Adaptive Deformable Convolution for Remote Sensing Object Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Modeling geometric variations, particularly the extreme fluctuations in scale and shape, stands as a persistent challenge in computer vision, which is significantly exacerbated in remote sensing object detection (RSOD). Existing methods are often constrained by the fixed geometric topology of standard convolutions or the insufficient representation power of linear feature aggregation, making it difficult to strike an ideal balance between adaptability and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a novel scale- and shape-adaptive method named Kernel Adaptive Deformable Convolution (KAD-Conv). Specifically, KAD-Conv employs a specialized Deformable Spatial Convolution (DSC) at its core to adaptively adjust sampling locations, while reformulating the mask generation process to fully leverage the mask's potential for discriminative feature modulation. In KAD-Conv, we further introduce a Scale-aware Kernel Adaptive mechanism, which enables the dynamic adjustment of sampling scales to effectively capture object representations across extreme scale variations without increasing kernel size. With KAD-Conv, we develop a novel object detection network based on Multi-task Guided Learning (MGL), called KAD-CNet. Extensive experiments conducted on widely used remote sensing benchmark datasets, including DOTA-v1.0, DIOR, and NWPU VHR-10, along with validation on natural scenes exhibiting extreme geometric variations, have validated the effectiveness of the proposed KAD-CNet. Moreover, comprehensive comparisons against various YOLO-series models further underscore the practical value and efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: GenHOI: Generalizing Text-driven 4D Human-Object Interaction Synthesis for Unseen Objects
HENet++: Hybrid Encoding and Multi-task Learning for 3D Perception and Planning in Autonomous Driving
Degradation-aware Infrared Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Infrared image super-resolution (IISR) is inherently more challenging than its visible-light counterpart due to the presence of structured, infrared-specific degradations, including thermal noise, fixed-pattern noise, and spatially non-uniform blur. These degradations deviate substantially from commonly assumed degradation models and often lead existing methods to produce unstable structures, amplified noise, or hallucinated textures. In this work, we present DIRSR, a degradation-aware framework for infrared image super-resolution that explicitly incorporates infrared degradation perception into the restoration process. The proposed approach characterizes instance-level infrared degradation conditions and leverages degradation-aware semantic guidance to regulate the trade-off between perceptual quality and structural fidelity. In addition, infrared imaging priors are embedded into a physics-informed, region-aware optimization objective to enhance foreground structural consistency while suppressing spurious background details. Extensive experiments on multiple public infrared benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative performance and visual quality, and further improves downstream infrared detection and segmentation tasks.

title: STRIDE: Continual Learning using Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding
abstract: Developing general-purpose physics-based character controllers via reinforcement learning is fundamentally hindered by policy interference in continuous spaces. While training isolated controllers avoids interference, it incurs significant training overhead and yields disjointed behavioral transitions. To address these challenges, we present STRIDE (Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding), a framework for the continual learning and composition of diverse character behaviors. Instead of training independent models, STRIDE leverages policy quantization via a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) to dynamically discover and encode reusable behavioral primitives within a discrete latent space. New behaviors and tasks are learned by combining existing codewords, providing a stable motion prior that structurally eliminates catastrophic forgetting. Evaluated across diverse locomotion styles, agile maneuvers like kicking, and composite tasks like target-aiming, STRIDE accelerates downstream learning by × 1.3 to × 2.0 compared to baseline learning frameworks. Furthermore, the discrete representations inherently improve policy interpretability, allowing direct tracking of skill activations and behavioral decisions during task execution. STRIDE offers a scalable, transparent solution for continual character control without compromising motion quality.

title: A multi-sensor framework for comparing and integrating optical, C-band and L-band SAR inundation products in tropical floodplain of Australia
abstract: Accurate inundated landscape mapping is essential for understanding hydrological connectivity, wetland dynamics and floodplain processes in tropical environments. However, optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sensors often produce inconsistent inundation estimates due to differences in sensor physics, wavelength sensitivity, vegetation and cloud penetration, and analytical methods.
